#1962. Rangers have discovered steely edge as late Fir Park drama offers glimpse of growing title-winning mentality

There was no disguising the satisfaction in Tuur Rommens' voice as he reflected on Rangers' late 2-1 victory over Motherwell. It provided the Belgian defender with further evidence of a team learning learning how to grind out results and develop a winning mentality to overcome hurdles when it matters most.

Rangers looked in danger of leaving Fir Park frustrated on Saturday night after a performance in which their attacking intent was not always matched by clinical finishing. Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen had done everything within his power to earn his side a point, producing a string of outstanding saves, but Rangers refused to settle for a draw.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Their persistence was eventually rewarded in the 88th minute when Ryan Naderi’s effort took a deflection off Martin Moorman, wrong-footing Paulsen and finding the net. Those heroics sparked jubilant celebrations among the sizeable travelling support.

Rommens acknowledged that such a dramatic conclusion in North Lanarkshire could provide a significant boost to morale inside the away dressing room, praising his team-mates' willingness to keep pushing despite facing a goalkeeper in inspired form.

“The spirit was good and especially when you score a goal in the last minute of the game, it always gives an extra boost,” said the left-back. “Everybody was very happy in the dressing room. It's never easy to come here and to win. Last year we didn't win here, so it's nice to come here and win and get the three points.

“We had a lot of chances. The finish was not always there, but we played a very good game. It feels like we've gained these two points. Their goalkeeper did an amazing job. It's not only our finishing, it's also credit that he saves a lot of shots. Of course, if it stays 1-1, you're thinking, ‘oh, come on, we need to get another one’. But at the end, we got what we deserved.”

Rangers were left to rue too many dropped points last season, and Rommens is acutely aware of how big the difference between settling for a point and claiming all three can be over the course of a campaign.

The connection between the players and supporters is another factor the 23-year-old believes is proving invaluable in helping Rangers navigate difficult moments.

“The fanbase is unbelievable. It doesn't feel like an away game because there are so many fans with us,” he added. “When you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they're so happy, we're so happy, so it gives us an extra boost to go again on Tuesday and try to get another win.”

Attention now turns to Rangers’ game in hand against Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night, with Derek McInnes’ side looking to capitalise on a run of three successive home fixtures and build on their 13-game unbeaten streak.

The bigger picture remains firmly in their sights, although Rommens is not interested in becoming distracted by the current state of the title race.

“It's been a long time (since we last played at Ibrox). So it will be nice to play in front of our fans again,” he said. “I think at home we have to maintain our good run. You just need to keep winning and at the end you'll see where you're at. But if you keep winning, you'll be up there.”

#1961. Tuttosport: Not just Endrick and Tresoldi – Milan eyeing Bundesliga striker Krösche admires

A new idea has emerged for AC Milan to strengthen their attack, and it is a player that incoming Head of Football Markus Krösche knows well.

This morning’s edition of Tuttosport writes that the two dreams for January are Nicolò Tresoldi and Endrick, but a third option is starting to emerge at Milan. The player is equally effective in terms of goals, but perhaps less media-burdened than Gonçalo Ramos.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese striker has just three goals so far for Milan since joining for a club-record €73m fee, and his current drought is now over one month. This is why finding a viable alternative in the winter is key, but perhaps without spending another €60-70m on another forward.

It will be very hard to snatch Tresoldi from Club Brugge during the winter transfer window, as Arsenal and Atletico Madrid are also strongly interested in him. Meanwhile, Endrick’s departure from Real Madrid is currently being vetoed by Jose Mourinho. So, who could the Rossoneri turn to?

Milan could look towards the Bundesliga, more specifically Stuttgart’s Ermedin Demirovic. He is a name highly regarded by Milan’s new Head of Football – Markus Krösche – who has watched him up close for several years.

The Bosnian striker’s contract expires in 2028, and there’s currently no agreement to extend it. Therefore, his price tag – despite an  excellent start to the season – isn’t likely to skyrocket and could become affordable.

He’s already scored nine goals across all competitions: five in nine appearances in the league, and four in four in the Champions League. That seems to provide enough evidence that the Bosnia international is ready for a top club.

Ermedin Demirovic has scored a hat-trick in the first 32 minutes of Stuttgart's game with Viking.

It's the fifth earliest in Champions League history:

🇵🇱 Robert Lewandowski vs. RB Salzburg (23rd minute)🇮🇹 Marco Simone vs. Rosenborg (24th minute)🇫🇷 Kylian Mbappe vs.… pic.twitter.com/V5XA1iEwLg

— The Athletic | Football (@TheAthleticFC) September 9, 2026

Demirovic is raring to go and is eyeing potential suitors (including several English clubs). A couple of years ago, Juventus sought him as a partner to Dusan Vlahovic , when Cristiano Giuntoli was still in charge. Now, that move to Italy might finally come about.

In recent weeks, the presence of Milan scouts at Stuttgart’s matches has not gone unnoticed. Demirovic has responded in his own way: with goals. Dzeko’s heir in the Bosnian national team can also play as a second striker and therefore, if necessary, partner Ramos.

In the past he has also been used as a winger in a three-man attack. This versatility is invaluable for a chameleon-like coach like Ruben Amorim, and it would allow Ermedin to be used in any type of situation.

It would also facilitate Francesco Camarda’s possible loan exit, so this is a situation well worth watching as we reach the weeks leading up to the winter window.

#1960. Fabian Hurzeler explains Georginio and Charalampos Kostoulas decision after Brighton loss at Hull City

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler revealed that Charalampos Kostoulas picked up a knock while on international duty with Greece.

Kostoulas - who has five goals in all competitions - has been Brighton’s main striker this term but was on the bench at the MKM Stadium as Georginio led the line in the 2-0 loss at Hull.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

“Because Kostoulas came back from the international break with a small issue,” said Hurzeler when asked why Georginio started ahead of Kostoulas.

“Therefore we had to make this decision, it wasn't a tactical decision, we had to take care of the health of the player.

”It's just a small issue, he came back from being with Greece, so something was there, but he didn't feel like 100 per cent.”

Hull pounced at the death as Oli McBurnie struck twice in added time to snatch a 2-0 victory against high-flying Brighton at the MKM Stadium.

Hurzeler’s side were dominant but could not find a way through, thwarted on several occasions by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Their push for an eighth victory of the season was then halted by Joao Costinha’s dismissal a minute from time and, from there, the wheels came off.

McBurnie bundled home a fine Hull move two minutes into stoppage time and the Tigers were not done there as the striker buried his fourth goal in as many matches to lift his side up to 11th.

Hurzeler added: "For 65 minutes we showed a good performance then we dropped our intensity, levels and standards. In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon a frustrating game but we have to keep going.

"We will analyse it. That's the process we follow. I always emphasize keep staying humble. We have to outwork the opponent otherwise the opponents are too good in the Premier League and that's what we have to do better next time."

Brighton, for the first time this season, seemed to run out of gas in the closing stages and the the Costinha sending off tipped the balance in Hull’s favour.

Hurzeler said: "Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role. We made a decision, at that moment, a wrong decision, but we will analyse it.

“My team was desperate to win it, of course, in certain elements be more patient, be more disciplined, be more structured.

“That's what we missed, not only in the last minutes, also in the minutes before, and again, we will analyse it and make it better.”

#1959. Louis Saha says Man Utd should have signed £65m former Chelsea star

Louis Saha believes Manchester United should have signed Nicolas Jackson before his £65million move from Chelsea to Aston Villa.

Jackson enjoyed a fast start to life at Chelsea, scoring 17 goals in all competitions during his first season at Stamford Bridge.

But the Senegalese striker failed to hit those heights during the 2024-25 campaign and Chelsea sent him on loan to Bayern Munich last season.

The performances of Joao Pedro complicated Jackson’s future upon his return from his loan in Germany, and a sale to Villa was eventually sanctioned, reuniting the 25-year-old with his former Villarreal boss Unai Emery.

Back under Emery’s tutelage, Jackson has returned to his best, with nine goals in 14 appearances so far this season.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

And Saha believes United missed a trick by not trying to sign Jackson over the summer, particularly given Benjamin Sesko’s injury woes, which have seen him miss large swathes of this campaign.

‘Nicolas Jackson is a player that I think Man Utd really missed out on because he’s an experienced striker who plays well under pressure,’ Saha told CasinoHawks.

‘Of course, he misses chances sometimes, but his work rate and ability to keep opposing centre-backs busy are vital for team balance.

‘Aston Villa have done really well with those two players, I would’ve loved them at Old Trafford.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Saha feels similarly about midfielder Leon Goretzka, who joined Villa on a free transfer from Bayern Munich this summer, with the Frenchman adding: ‘Leon Goretzka was a bargain for Aston Villa.

‘There’s a bit of jealousy seeing someone like Goretzka go to Aston Villa while Man Utd lose Casemiro. You definitely need experienced players in that central area.

‘Adapting to the Premier League isn’t always easy, but Villa went for proven quality. It’s frustrating, as those are the types of opportunities Man United should be capitalizing on.’

#1958. Rocks’ first-half double hurts Hayes and Yeading

It was a second league win in a row after a shaky spell of results and left Danny Hollands’ men third in the table and just three points behind leaders Egham.

Early on Hayes’ Ben Shroll put a low ball into the area but Kaylen Hinds shot over from the edge of the box.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Roberts put Bognor in the lead as his run down the left saw him beat his marker before coolly sliding it under Rhys Forster in the Hayes goal on eight minutes.

Amari Fashanu won a corner for the visitors with his low strike but Benny Read headed it out. Liam Ferdinand created an opening but missed his chace in front of goal.

For the Rocks, Henry Nevill hooked a cross in from the left but Callum Laycock looped it up into the air with his head. Lennie Smith sped down the right but his cross-shot was saved.

Bognor extended their lead on 25 minutes when Roberts' shot was pushed out only as far as McDonald, who diverted it into the net on the rebound, despite Forster getting something on it.

From McDonald's corner, Tommy Block was denied in a crowded penalty area. On 38 minutes Joshua Edwards had to receive treatment as he took a bash to the head in a challenge with Laycock.

Smith got on the breakaway for Bognor and he fed McDonald, who struck a shot wide along the deck. Harry Grant blasted over as Hayes were very wasteful in front of goal.

Four minutes after the break, a fierce ball in from Dernell Wynter saw Ferdinand divert it in from close range to make it 2-1.

Shroll got another dangerous ball into the box but Amos Nasha's header was directed straight at Tommy Scott. Shroll went into the book for a shoulder barge into the back of Smith. Kaya Tshaka's free-kick picked out Block but his header was saved.

Tshaka swiped at a chance of his own and he had to come off injured. Ethan Robb replaced him.

Nevill blazed a cross from the left too high before Fashanu hit a curling effort with his right foot and Scott palmed it out. Fashanu hit a corner deep towards the back post with Shroll under it, but Laycock and Scott combined to keep it out.

Nasha did well to pass the ball to Ferdinand and he hit the right post with his low effort on 69 minutes. Roberts was replaced by Ben Anderson for the Rocks and Nasha went into the book as he pulled Nevill back.

Scott pulled out a wonderful save down to his right to keep Grant’s low volleyed effort from just outside the area. Ferdinand was offside on the rebound.

Ollie Lovell came off on 80 minutes for Bognor, then the referee pulled up injured with a strained calf so Bognor's public address announcer, Peter Kelly-Sullivan, had to take up the flag for linesman’s duty for the remainder of the game.

Brendan Matthew had a header diverted wide when he had the goal at his mercy in the 94th minute.

It was a nervy final moments for the Rocks with the visitors always a danger but they held on for the win.

Next up is the highly-anticipated game away to Jersey Bulls – and over 200 Bognor fans are expected to make the trip to the island on Saturday.

#1957. Man Utd chief Omar Berrada breaks silence on Man City charges and denies involvement

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted he was not involved ‘in any wrongdoings’ during his time at Manchester City amid the ongoing case against his former employers.

An independent commission found City guilty of breaching more than 100 of the Premier League’s financial rules in September between the period of 2009 and 2018.

City have appealed against the ruling and repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

Berrada joined United in January 2024 having spent over a decade working in various roles for City Football Group.

He was named the club’s CEO in 2016 and remained in that role until 2020 when he was named City Football Group’s chief football operations officer for the next four years.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Berrada’s time at the club’s CEO overlaps with the period in which City were investigated. But the United chief has no concerns over any implications for him in the case.

‘I’m not concerned,’ Berrada told Sky Sports.

‘I want to be very clear about this: I wasn’t involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn’t involved in the proceedings. There are no allegations against me.

‘In that sense, there will be no surprises.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Asked whether United could look to pursue compensation if City fail in their appeal, Berrada replied: ‘I don’t want to comment on that because right now, it’s an ongoing process.

‘When it runs its course, then we’ll take a view on what is our position as Manchester United.’

Berrada and the rest of United’s hierarchy have just presided over their third mid-season managerial sacking in three years with Mauricio Pochettino the latest to be tasked with lifting the club from its malaise.

‘If you think about the fact that we’ve had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven’t achieved the stability that we want to – that’s for sure,’ Berrada said.

‘There are different circumstances as to why it didn’t work out with Erik, Ruben and now Michael. And we’re always learning. We’re always trying to improve and understand what has failed.’

#1956. Man City charges claim shot down as Enzo Maresca sent warning before Fulham (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 08:00

Uncertainty over Manchester City's 115 charges is without question a contributing factor to their Premier League struggles, former Sky Blues midfielder Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Enzo Maresca's side will endeavour to avoid a fourth consecutive defeat in the top flight when they host Fulham on Saturday lunchtime, having lost to Nottingham Forest, Brighton & Hove Albion and Aston Villa before the international break.

Man City's dire run of form has seen them slip six points behind Arsenal at the top of the Premier League table, while also falling below high-flying Brighton into third position, and they are just three points clear of Liverpool in fourth.

As Maresca's men try to focus on on-field matters, the appeal over their guilty verdict is a highly unwelcome distraction, and the threat of unprecedented sanctions looms if their charges are upheld.

Maresca has denied that the charges are a distraction, but Hamann - who made 71 appearances for the Citizens - has shot down the manager's claim and believes that the off-field concerns are impacting the club's performances.

"Nobody seems to know what's going to happen," Hamann said. "One person says they get off with the charges, the other says they get deducted 70 points. Everything and anything is possible. If they were to deduct 60 or 70 points, they would have to play in the Championship next season.

"I don't think many of the players, apart from maybe one or two who say they will stick it out, would want to stay. Probably 90 to 95% of the players will want to leave the club, and at some stage it has to have an effect.

"I'm a bit surprised it came so quickly after that. Maybe it's not the only reason, but it's certainly a reason they haven't played that well because they started the season really well. They played a fantastic game against Paris at home, even though they got beaten. It was the game of the season for me.

"It was absolutely thrilling and fantastic for both teams. I think it had an effect, and it may continue to have an effect. Uncertain times at City at the moment."

It has now been almost two months since the Premier League confirmed that Man City had been found guilty of all financial charges, and the verdict prompted an immediate appeal.

The appeal process must be concluded within 12 weeks, and the expectation is that the hearing will take place in mid-December ahead of a potential verdict in early January.

In the meantime, Premier League chiefs have supposedly contacted clubs to seek legal protection in case any of Man City's sponsors decide to sue; 14 clubs must approve the motion for it to pass.

Elsewhere, Man City owner Sheikh Mansour has reportedly seen a £1.5bn deal with a US investment firm collapse, thus denying City Football Group extra liquidity as the uncertainty rumbles on.

#1955. Derby draw ‘bittersweet’ for Sevilla boss Garcia

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Sevilla boss Luis Garcia feels his team were by far the better team against Real Betis, labelling their last-gasp draw as a "bittersweet" result.

Kike Salas netted late on in Saturday's derby to snatch a 1-1 draw for Sevilla, who fell behind to Antony's effort early in the second half.

Sevilla had 25 shots to Betis' six, and accumulated chances worth 2.3 expected goals to their opponent's 0.6.

They registered 47 touches in the Betis box and also hit the woodwork, though Garcia's team did fail to create a big chance.

And Garcia said a point was the least Sevilla deserved.

"We drew at the end, and it's a tremendous joy, but we all have a bittersweet feeling, because we were much better [than Betis]," he said.

"We had 25 shots on goal compared to just six, playing in the opposition's half, creating more scoring opportunities.

"I think it's one of the matches we dominated the most."

Hang it in the Louvre https://t.co/6XAiWr0YwU

— Sevilla FC (@SevillaFC_ENG) November 22, 2026

Garcia did concede, though, that Sevilla are lacking real quality up top.

"We're lacking talent up front, not from the forwards themselves, but moments of inspiration in the final third," he added.

"Football is about quality; it's about the difference in talent. But the team deserves respect. We keep adding points and fighting until the end.

"I respect [Betis coach] Manuel [Pellegrini] because I'm fond of him, and coaches come to press conferences wearing their team's shirt, but if anyone deserved to win, it was Sevilla."

Betis defender Marc Bartra, however, felt Sevilla got lucky, as he claimed Salas should have been sent off for an earlier tackle on Isco.

"It's clear we deserved to take all three points, absolutely," Bartra said.

"They equalised with a player who should have been sent off. I prefer to focus on how the team performed.

"It was clear he stepped on Isco's foot. I saw it live and on replay. The images speak for themselves. For this to happen at this stage with all the cameras, I'd rather not say what I really think."

#1953. Omar Berrada hits back at criticism over Manchester United’s transfer strategy

Manchester United’s CEO Omar Berrada has hit back at criticism of the club’s transfer strategy last summer and insists a ‘disciplined’ approach is required.

United spent £155 million on signing three midfielders in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba in the summer transfer window.

However, Mauricio Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford this week without a recognised striker as Benjamin Sesko is out for the remainder of the year with a shin problem, while Luke Shaw has missed United’s last seven games due to injury.

United supporters have criticised the club’s decision to only strengthen Michael Carrick’s midfield in the summer but Berrada is adamant the squad is ‘fundamentally better’ after their signings.

‘You have to take it in the context of the last few years,’ Berrada told Sky Sports.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The summer of 2025, I think the recruitment team was widely praised with the four players that were signed. And they did very well. They helped the team achieve Champions League qualification.

‘When we look at this summer, we went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play. It’s probably been the summer or the transfer window where there’s been the highest inflation in transfer fees.

‘And we’ve said publicly and we’ve said consistently in the last few years that we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players for the right value at the right time in terms of what the squad needs.

‘And when we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we’re receiving a lot of criticism for it but we’re actually happy with the players that we bought.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, and let’s not forget that we’ve also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona – these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.

‘It’s true that we lost Casemiro, who is a top player and gave a lot to the club. We also lost Manuel Ugarte to, unfortunately, an ACL injury. So our focus was very much about straightening the midfield.

‘When we started the transfer window, we really only had Kobbie Mainoo as our midfielder. So we wanted to reinforce that, and we did it.’

Berrada also addressed United’s decision not to sign a new left-sided defender after the club made an enquiry for Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

‘When you look at the other areas of the pitch, and there’s a lot of discussion about the back line,’ Berrada said.

‘But we did come into it thinking we have depth. We have nine players that can play in the back line, in the back four positions.

‘So that’s why we looked primarily at investing in the midfield. But we were always looking for opportunities. I think it’s been widely reported that we were looking at potentially the left-back position as a reinforcement.

‘I think what we’ve seen in the back line is we’ve had injuries, it’s taken Matthijs de Ligt longer than we would want it to get back. Unfortunately, Luke Shaw suffered a muscle injury that meant he was out for five or six weeks.

‘So could we have signed an additional defender to straighten the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players and you have to find the right players at the right value.

‘There’s no point in us spending £40 million, £50m for players that we’re not convinced are going to add value to the team.

‘So it’s always about being disciplined and finding the right opportunities and getting the right players that are going to take us forward.

‘When I talk about being disciplined, I talk about not overspending on players that don’t necessarily add quality to the team.

‘Because when you sign a player that doesn’t work out for Man Utd, it becomes very difficult to move that player on or to get the sale we want. And that can set us back.

‘So when I talk about being disciplined, I’m not talking about necessarily not spending to get the top players. We have the ambition to win, to win the Premier League, to win the Champions League, to win the domestic cups. And for that, we need top talent. So when we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don’t want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it.’

#1952. GdS: A red-hot start and the ‘S’ word – the data that inspires confidence in Amorim

A statistic has been doing the rounds regarding Ruben Amorim’s league record with AC Milan, which is gathering some attention.

His style of play is open to criticism, his selections are controversial, his words are regularly quite strong and he’s often called into question at the first sign of failure. For Amorim, his first months with the Rossoneri have been a rollercoaster ride.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been ups and downs: things have been better domestically, culminating in a derby victory over Inter, but in the Europa League the one win from four games means the Rossoneri currently sit outside the playoff zone.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, there is a key bit of data to contextualise things. With 24 points in his first 11 Serie A matches, Amorim is averaging 2.18 points per game, the result of seven wins, three draws, and one defeat.

It is the highest ever for a Milan coach in the three-point era, ahead of Stefano Pioli, Carlo Ancelotti and Massimiliano Allegri. Looking at coaches with at least five stints in the Italian top flight, only Antonio Conte boasts a better figure than the Portuguese coach, with 2.21 points per game.

This is obviously an unfair comparison, given that the former Napoli coach’s points average takes into account all 279 of his Serie A games – with spells at Atalanta, Juventus, Inter and Napoli – compared to just 11 for the former United manager.

However, it is a testament to the excellent work done thus far by Amorim and his staff. Even more so in a season in which the decision was made to undertake a revolution in several respects, to relaunch a team and a fan base that had been burned by the collapse of last season.

Gerry Cardinale and the ownership made significant investments during the last transfer window, spending €70m on Goncalo Ramos and €50m on Diego Moreira, plus €25m on Mario Gila. This is also why Milan fans have high expectations for Amorim’s era.

To date, the average from these first 11 games project the Rossoneri to land around 83 points by the end of the season. Last year, Inter won the Scudetto with 87 points, and 71 were needed to finish fourth, the minimum target set by the owners.

Allegri’s Milan stopped at 70 points, despite a strong start to the season that even fuelled a few Scudetto dreams for a few months. That start, however, was inferior to this season: a year ago, after 11 matchdays, AC Milan had 22 points, two fewer than under Amorim.

It is an encouraging beginning to the new era that fans hope will translate into concrete results, perhaps even the Scudetto, a target announced by owner Cardinale as a real aim, as unrealistic as it may have seemed before a ball was kicked.

Amorim is trying to convey his vision of football and instil a more European mentality in his team, and the numbers so far – at least in the league – seem to prove him right. To find a better start to a season one must rewind to 2022-23, when Milan had 26 points from 11 games under Pioli.

Ruben Amorim has the highest points-per-game average of any #ACMilan coach in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era: 2.18 over 11 matches.

Among all coaches with 5+ stints in the league during that period, only Antonio Conte (2.21) has a higher average.

[via @OptaPaolo] pic.twitter.com/jwPLgVw0z7

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 19, 2026

Speaking of Pioli, in the specific ranking of Milan coaches with the highest points average – led by Amorim, as mentioned – the coach who led the Rossoneri to their 19th Scudetto (2021-22) occupies second place at 2.02 points per game in 183 Serie A matches.

Pioli also achieved the best start in Milan’s history: in the Scudetto year, he earned 31 points from the opening 11 games, the result of 10 wins and 1 draw, with a record average of 2.82 points per game.

In third place among Milan coaches with the highest points average is Ancelotti, with 1.95 points in 283 Serie A games as Milan coach. Allegri is just off the podium, with 1.91 points in 172 games across his two spells at the club.

To compare Amorim with two of his compatriots who recently worked at Milanello, Paulo Fonseca averaged just 1.59 points per game from 17 games, while Sergio Conceicao fared slightly better with 1.71 points in 21 games.

In short, Amorim’s performance is encouraging, but still relative given the very limited sample size. A crucial month is now beginning for Milan: a seven-game tour de force before Christmas that will reveal a lot about the true ambitions of the coach and his team, with form in Europe to fix.

#1951. Five alive: Bexhill move on up with win over Midhurst

Since Bexhill secured a win in the reverse fixture in September, Midhurst have struggled to recover from internal strife that saw their manager and a number of players depart, with a run of poor results that has plunged them into the relegation mire.

Meanwhile, Bexhill have managed to strike a rich vein of form with a squad that blends youth with experience and a strong sense of togetherness and solidarity.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Missing Luke Donaldson with a three-match ban, Pirates gaffer Jay Skinner-Swain kept Ash Latuske and Ryan Moir in their attacking positions on the flanks with Charlie Scarles slotting into an advanced role in midfield.

Bexhill couldn’t have hoped for a better start. In the first minute Theo Coombs had a chance well saved but from the resulting corner Charlie Playford ghosted into the six yard box to beat all-comers with a bullet header from point blank range.

Three minutes later Latuske beat two men with a powerful run down the right to set up Shonk and the Bexhill record goalscorer made no mistake in adding another to his tally.

It looked like Bexhill would run amok but it’s all credit to the young Midhurst lads that they didn’t just fold. They put in some decent enough approach moves but the Pirates defence had the measure of them.

At the other end, another goal looked almost inevitable. On 25 minutes Shonk had an effort cleared off the line from a Moir corner. Shortly after, Scarles had an effort well saved by the young Midhurst keeper who was keeping his side in with a sniff.

Just before the break there was nothing he could do though as Latuske lashed in a drive that had the keeper beaten all ends up but the ball somehow bounced back out into play off the inside of the post.

Bexhill went in two goals to the good at half-time but on the balance of play and chances it should have been more.

Almost inevitably Midhurst delivered a scare early in the second half. Just five minutes in, a runner skipped past the Bexhill defensive lines and delivered a ball which was swept into the Pirates net. It was followed minutes later by a good effort that required a fine save from Finn Holter.

But the moment soon passed for Midhurst and Bexhill got back in amongst it. The killer goal came on 55 and it was that man Coombs again, benefitting from some more great play from Latuske and swivelling to tuck the chance away.

Now it really was all Bexhill as Midhurst wilted under the pressure. On 65 minutes Latuske was at it again, this time setting up Shonk, whose shot curled just wide of the post. It was the briefest of respites for Midhurst as Moir played in Coombs on the left and this time he turned provider, chipping in a perfect cross for Shonk to nod home for 4-1.

Bexhill were rampant now and on 76 minutes substitute Jack Samways wrapped it up at 5-1 to the Pirates with the pick of the afternoon’s goals. Winning the ball just inside the box he crashed a perfect half volley into the Brockley Road End net.

It was no less than Bexhill deserved for a thoroughly professional demolition job on their hapless visitors.

The Pirates move up sixth in the league and have a chance to keep their current run going with the long trip over to Pagham on Saturday afternoon.

#1947. Antonio Conte sends message to Man Utd after missing out on Mauricio Pochettino’s job

Antonio Conte has played down suggestions he missed out on the Manchester United job because of his demanding reputation in management.

United made their third mid-season managerial change in three years after sacking Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino coming in as his replacement earlier this month.

Conte was among the names initially explored along with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann. The Italian, a free agent since parting ways with Napoli, was thought to be keen on the role at Old Trafford but it was widely reported United had reservations over some of his methods.

The Italian led Juventus, Chelsea, Inter Milan and Napoli to league titles but has not lasted longer than two seasons at any club since leaving the Bianconeri in 2014.

Conte has a reputation for being hugely demanding with players and the board but in an interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio he insisted anyone scared of his approach is scared of winning.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The coach recalled a meeting with Sir Alex Ferguson during his time in charge of Chelsea, praising the standards the Scot said before insisting the idea United no longer want to meet those standards is ‘offensive’

‘If someone is scared of my method, then they’re scared of winning, because that methodology leads to winning,’ Conte said.

‘That’s my answer. United has such an important history that it seems strange to imagine anyone being scared of a job aimed at restoring the club to its former glory.

They last won the championship in 2013, under Ferguson. I have enormous respect for Sir Alex Ferguson. I’ve read his book, and when I was in London, I was lucky enough to go to his house and spend a day with him. He’s incredibly eager to talk about football, even if it’s sometimes hard to understand his Scottish accent.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘With his method and his approach, he made Manchester United great. That’s why I find certain words about United almost offensive: it’s like vetoing a return to their own history. The method is needed to achieve important results.

‘If you then tell me that it’s a method that needs work, I’d say yes: everyone needs to work, not just the players.’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Paris Saint-Germain confirmed Desire Doue has ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee and will undergo surgery.

Luis Enrique confirmed after the match that it was a "serious injury" and PSG have said Doue will undergo surgery before the end of November.

#1945. Fabian Hurzeler reveals what frustrated him most about Brighton's defeat at Hull

The Seagulls looked on course for at least a point at the MKM Stadium, before two stoppage-time goals from Oli McBurnie condemned them to defeat.

Hurzeler – who was booked by the referee late on in the match – felt Brighton had been the better side for much of the contest. But he criticised their performance after the opening 65 minutes, admitting they had allowed Hull back into the game.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Speaking to Match of the Day, he said: "For 65 minutes we showed a good performance then we chopped our intensity, levels and standards.

"In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon, a frustrating game but we have to keep going."

Brighton were reduced to ten men in the 89th minute, when Costinha received a second yellow card for pushing Sorba Thomas to the ground.

McBurnie then struck in the 92nd and 95th minutes to secure all three points for Hull.

Asked whether the dismissal had contributed to the late goals, Hurzeler said: "Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role."

The Brighton boss also acknowledged the outstanding performance of Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who made several important saves to keep his side in the game.

"We have to give credit to him. He made a good performance but in the end it's our responsibility," Hurzeler said.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Hurzeler described Hull's opening goal as a ‘lucky punch’ but insisted Brighton had to take responsibility for the result.

"That's football. The Premier League is ruthless. Hull scored with a lucky punch, we have to accept it and be better next time.”

He suggested his players had become impatient as they struggled to make their chances count.

"We rushed things, we lost a bit of intensity, we tried to force things because we weren't patient enough," he said.

"For 65 minutes we could easily win the game.

"You can easily get frustrated if you miss so many chances."

Hurzeler was also full of praise for Tzolakis, describing him as a ‘great goalkeeper’ who had produced a ‘big performance’.

The Brighton manager was asked about a penalty appeal involving Pascal Gross but said he had not watched the incident back.

"The referee wasn't the reason why we lost today.”

Hurzeler insisted his team would analyse what went wrong but stressed the importance of maintaining their standards in the Premier League.

"We will analyse it – that's the process we follow," he told Match of the Day.

"I always emphasize keep staying humble. We have to outwork the opponent otherwise the opponents are too good in the Premier League and that's what we have to do better next time."

Harry Kane is facing several months out after suffering an ankle ligament injury during Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga game on Friday night.

#1943. Monza vs Fiorentina - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 21 Nov 2026 09:32

Both battling at the wrong end of the Serie A standings, Monza and Fiorentina will vie for three precious points when matchday 12 comes to a close on Monday night.

While the hosts have slumped into the drop zone after four consecutive defeats, their Viola visitors are showing signs of revival.

Having lost six of their first eight games and recalled their former interim manager, Fiorentina had begun to steady the ship before international football intervened.

Paolo Vanoli's side have inched away from the relegation zone by claiming five points from their last three outings, with an away victory over Sassuolo being sandwiched by a pair of 2-2 home draws.

After sharing the spoils with Atalanta at the end of October, the Viola fought hard for a draw against old foes Juventus, taking the lead twice before settling for one point.

Both acceptable results in isolation, but Fiorentina's struggles at Stadio Franchi show no sign of ending: the Tuscan club's last league win on home turf dates back to April.

Now bound for Brianza, their two top-flight wins this term have both come on the road, so they will hope to pick up another on Monday.

However, sitting just two points above Monza, Fiorentina have yet to keep a clean sheet in Serie A and continue to look vulnerable at the back.

Across seven prior meetings in Monza, there have been three wins apiece, but the hosts have won two of the last three.

While precedent may suggest that they will come out on top, the Brianzoli departed for the international break on a dismal run of form.

Consecutive defeats to Torino, Napoli, Bologna and Atalanta left them stuck inside the drop zone, abruptly halting a relatively promising start.

Only Sassuolo have conceded more goals after 11 matchdays, leaving head coach Ivan Juric searching for solutions to his team's defensive woes.

Failing to score for the first time this season, the Serie B playoff winners were beaten 1-0 by La Dea last time out, continuing a grim top-flight record at Stadio Brianteo.

Dating back to their relegation campaign of 2024-25, Monza have won just three of their last 24 home games in Serie A.

Although expensive summer signing Arthur Atta is set to end a six-match absence, Fiorentina are still missing Fabiano Parisi and Marin Pongracic due to injury.

Alieu Njie returned from Sweden duty with a minor thigh problem, so Wilfried Gnonto or Pedro Goncalves could be promoted from the bench if required.

As part of an attacking trio, Njie has racked up five goal involvements from his last three Serie A appearances, while Argentine pair Mateo Pellegrino and Franco Mastantuono both have four goals this season.

Meanwhile, one man has been carrying Monza's attack: Capocannoniere leader and Liverpool target Gustavo Varela has scored more than half of their 17 league goals, netting nine in 10 games.

In the three-points-for-a-win era, only Fiorentina legend Gabriel Batistuta (13) and David Trezeguet of Juventus (10) have topped his tally for a newly promoted side after 11 matchdays.

Monza captain Matteo Pessina returned to full training during the break, having missed most of the campaign so far.

Former Fiorentina midfielder Michael Folorunsho has also recovered from a calf problem, but Yvan Maye and Jay Robinson are both doubts.

Tornqvist; Kouadio, Goglichidze, Lucchesi; Birindelli, Akinsanmiro, Foe Ondoa, Mangas; Mota, Robinson; Varela

De Gea; Jimenez, Dragusin, Viery, Mario; Ndour, Fagioli, Oulai; Mastantuono, Pellegrino, Gnonto

Fiorentina have equalled their worst defensive start to any Serie A season -  a negative record set back in 1933 - while Monza have never conceded more at this stage of a top-flight campaign.

They will surely share several goals on Monday night, but the Viola's vibrant attack should secure maximum points.

#1942. Musah lifts lid on Amorim’s faith, early career, preferred role and Scudetto ‘ambition’

Yunus Musah has insisted that AC Milan must believe in the Scudetto, while also assessing his start to the campaign under Ruben Amorim.

Going into the summer, an uncertain fate awaited Musah. Massimiliano Allegri did not see him as a part of the plans for 2025-26 and so he was loaned to Atalanta, where he had a mixed year and ultimately returned as they did not use their option to buy him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Many sources presumed that it would be a return in passing and that a new destination would be found, but Amorim had other plans. The new coach clearly saw something in the USA international, and he has become a regular starter regardless of the system used.

Such is his importance, there is even talk of a renewal being discussed. Musah was interviewed by SportMediaset and it was published two days before the Serie A campaign resumes with a home game against Frosinone. His comments were transcribed by MilanNews.

Do you feel like a ‘wild card’ for Milan?

“A little less so this year because I haven’t changed positions as much, even though I can do that. I’ve been able to play in midfield and improve in that area.”

“I think he watched my old games, because he already knew what he expected from me and what he could ask of me. He did his homework, he watched everything, and he already knew what and how he could use me.”

We’ve never seen you play left-back at Milan like you did in Genoa: how did this idea come about?

“I don’t know (laughs). This question is for the coach. Bartesaghi and Estupinan are very good, but that day he wanted a right-footed player on the left.”

If it were up to you, where do you want to play most?

“I think playing in midfield. Not fixed, though, being able to go anywhere so I can get the ball, get deep, without being fixed.”

Do you think Milan is improving? Is the Scudetto possible?

“It’s possible. We train every day for it. We all have the dream and ambition of winning it, and we’ll do everything we can to get there.”

Can you tell us what you remember about your time in the States?

“Playing for the United States helped me gain this sense of belonging. Until I was 17, I only had a passport, but now I feel part of the culture.”

“I can go there. I know the restaurants, the chains, the people from different states, the geography. I understand American people so much now.

“I have many passports, I lived and grew up in many countries, like here in Italy, in England, so I feel a bit of everything.”

Have you ever returned to see your childhood homes?

“Yes, in 2021 I returned to New York. I saw the house where I lived that year. The Bronx. It was beautiful to see it. There was a piece missing from my memory, and it was nice to be able to connect it.”

“Yes. I left him with the neighbours in Valencia because I couldn’t take him to Milan.”

“My family was already in Italy, and my mother had to go back and forth to America.”

What was your childhood like in Castelfranco Veneto?

“Beautiful. It’s a place where my parents weren’t afraid to let me play all day outside in the parking lot near the apartment building.”

Is it true that your parents’ years of financial sacrifice were years of financial hardship?

“Of course. Obviously, when I grew up, we weren’t rich, we didn’t have much money, but from the time I left home, even when I was little, my parents never let me go without anything. I hope I’m their pride, because they are mine.”

You have also played for Arsenal and Valencia. What were the transitions like?

“Playing for Arsenal was a great privilege, because I arrived from Italy at 9 years old, played with a small team, and immediately joined Arsenal.

“I was ready to move to the first team when I was 16, and Valencia had a plan for me. I spent four wonderful years in Spain; it’s a city that will always remain in my heart.”

What’s the atmosphere like in the dressing room?

“Last year I watched them a lot; they were a very solid team and difficult to beat. Amorim brought a very positive vibe, we understand each other. He understands the player very well and vice versa.

“It helps when he understands what the players need; he’s good at that, and the players in the team are pretty calm.”

Is he someone who gets angry when necessary?

“Yes. After Ferencvaros he was very angry, like everyone else.”

“My wife is from Zanzibar, my family is Ghanaian. So it’s nice to travel to our home countries in the summer.”

#1941. Bayern Munich board member claims ‘no club would buy’ Jamal Musiala due to health condition

Bayern Munich’s supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested Jamal Musiala may be offered a pay cut due to his health situation and claims no club would buy the midfielder ‘under these conditions’.

The 23-year-old collapsed in two different games in the space of four days during Bayern’s pre-season campaign in the summer.

Musiala later revealed that he had been suffering from ‘brief, temporary – but treatable – absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction’.

The midfielder also suffered a thigh injury in September and made his return from his two-month absence on Friday night as Bayern drew 1-1 with FC Koln.

Speaking after the game, Rummenigge insisted Bayern must consider their financial situation with Musiala on a contract which is worth in excess of €25 million (£20.9m) a year and expires in 2030.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘What we know unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level he has so often shown here in the stadium,’ Rummenigge told Sky Germany.

‘We need to talk to the family, the player, and the agency, because then these sums of money, sorry, with all due respect, are no longer feasible.

‘I cannot imagine that Jamal wants to leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions.

‘We are all interested in his return, ideally in top form. But what happens if that isn’t the case? Then we still have to think about the finances.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The discussion hasn’t taken place yet. These are just ideas at this stage.’

Speaking earlier this month, Bayern’s honorary president, Uli Hoeness, also raised questions about Musiala’s contract due to his health issue.

‘We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,’ Hoeness said.

‘But whether he ​will have the same performance potential that he had… imagine if Bayern were now to question ‌his ⁠contract and say that what he is capable of delivering now is no longer what is in the contract.’

When asked about the assessment of Musiala’s by the club’s hierarchy, Bayern head coach Vincent Kompany said: ‘I have a very clear role in this club, as a coach, I have to believe in my players and that we can achieve something together.

‘If Jamal finds his level and form again, and we manage to do that together, then everyone wins – Bayern, the fans, and I believe German football as a whole. Because Jamal is a special player.

‘That is my role, quite clearly. If a coach does something different or says something different, then there is a problem, in my opinion.’

#1940. Man United transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino target 'flattered' by fresh Old Trafford links

By Darren Plant | 21 Nov 2026 09:36

Galatasaray forward Victor Osimhen is allegedly 'flattered' by speculation linking him to Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first Red Devils fixture on Sunday when his team face Liverpool at Anfield.

There is an argument that United need to enter the transfer market for a new left-back and centre-back over any other position.

However, with Benjamin Sesko sidelined in the long term, consideration will be given to adding a fresh face to the attack.

According to The Sun, Osimhen would be interested in taking an opportunity to move to Old Trafford.

The report claims that the Nigeria international is 'flattered' by suggestions that United could make a fresh move for his signature.

Osimhen has been linked with a transfer to the Premier League in the past, only for his wage demands or asking price at Napoli to allegedly provide a stumbling block.

Nevertheless, it is said that the 27-year-old still has ambitions to move to English football at some stage of his career.

As it stands, his contract at Galatasaray - which runs until the summer of 2029 - is likely to prevent any transfer from occurring in January.

That is seemingly partly a consequence of no release clause being present in his contract, while Galatasaray will not want to weaken their position in the Super Lig title race.

Ten goals and three assists have been contributed in his 11 appearances in Turkey's top flight and the Champions League this season.

Man United CEO Omar Berrada said in an interview with Sky Sports News this week that the club had been "disciplined" in the transfer market, and that is expected to remain the case.

Not only is Osimhen said to be on a contract at Galatasaray in the region of £13m per year, his club would demand in excess of £50m for his signature as a bare minimum.

United are unlikely to be able to afford those terms at this time, particularly when it is apparent that other positions need strengthening.

#1938. ‘Unbelievable’ Tzolakis key to Hull’s win over Brighton

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Oli McBurnie conceded Hull City "rode their luck" during their 2-0 win over Brighton, but he lauded goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis for his "unbelievable" display.

Hull ended an eight-game winless run in the Premier League, but they were put through their paces to claim all three points.

Tzolakis made a string of impressive saves to deny Diego Gomez, Georginio Rutter and Pascal Gross during the first half, with Lewis Dunk also repelled after the break.

A late turning point came when Brighton defender Costinha saw red for a second bookable offence, with Hull's threat on the counter-attack eventually proving fruitful in stoppage time.

McBurnie bundled home in the 92nd minute before tucking in his second following Mohamed Belloumi's cross to cap an eventful ending.

But Hull's matchwinner hailed Tzolakis as the key man for the Tigers.

"It doesn't feel like that to be fair. We haven't lost a game at home. They are a top team, and we knew it was going to be tough," McBurnie told Sky Sports.

"We rode our luck, and we have the big man [Tzolakis] to keep the ball out of the net, so that's what he's done.

"He [Tzolakis] was unbelievable. He has been all season for us to be fair to him. We give him a bit of stick about his gear, but he's been good in net.

"He was fantastic, kept us in the game today. We know if we are always in games we fancy ourselves getting chances and that's what we did."

1.75 – Brighton's xG is the most by any side in a half of football without scoring in the Premier League this season (from 10 shots in the first half). Tzolakis. https://t.co/o4XXK4pgWw

Hull scored two 90th-minute goals in the same Premier League game for the first time.

McBurnie's brace was his first in the competition on his 107th appearance, helping Hull remain unbeaten at home in the Premier League this season (W2 D4).

It is their longest unbeaten start at home in a league campaign since 2015-16 (first eight), and Tzolakis insisted it was a team effort rather than an individual one.

"So many saves but two goals from Oli [McBurnie]. It was a team effort and everyone helped each other," Tzolakis added.

"We are a unit here like a team. We play for each other. We saw a very good team effort, and we deserved to take the three points.

"In the first half we suffered a lot, but we managed the second half and scored two goals in transition, two goals from Oli and that's it."

Brighton, meanwhile, missed the chance to close the gap to Premier League leaders Arsenal, who were held to a 2-2 draw by Newcastle United on Saturday.

The Seagulls have now lost two of their last three Premier League games against newly promoted opposition (W1), while it was their third top-flight defeat due to winning goals scored in the 90th minute or later in 2026, their most such losses in a single calendar year.

McBurnie's first goal came just two minutes and 33 seconds after Costinha's dismissal.

"For 65 minutes we showed a good performance, then we changed our intensity, levels and standards," Fabian Hurzeler told BBC Match of the Day.

"In the Premier League they can punish you, especially after a red card. Overall, a frustrating game but we have to keep going. We will analyse it. That's the process we follow.

"I always emphasise staying humble. We have to outwork the opponent, otherwise the opponents are too good in the Premier League and that's what we have to do better."

#1935. Harry Kane injury could force Bayern Munich into £44m transfer dilemma amid Arsenal, Man United interest

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 09:39

Bayern Munich could be forced to reconsider their January transfer plans following Harry Kane's serious ankle injury, with a highly rated striker already on their radar also attracting interest from Arsenal and Manchester United.

The Bundesliga champions have confirmed that the England captain will miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during Friday's 1-1 draw with FC Koln.

The 33-year-old was withdrawn after just 20 minutes, leaving Vincent Kompany without his first-choice centre-forward at a crucial stage of the campaign. The setback is particularly concerning given Bayern's limited options in the position and their demanding domestic and European schedule.

One player who could now become increasingly relevant to the German club's recruitment discussions is Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, who has been monitored by Bayern scouts in recent weeks.

However, the 22-year-old's reported valuation of up to €50m (£44m), combined with Brugge's reluctance to sanction a winter departure, presents a significant obstacle should Bayern decide to bring forward their search for attacking reinforcements.

According to German newspaper TZ, Bayern have sent scouts to Belgium on several occasions to monitor Tresoldi, whose performances have attracted considerable attention across Europe.

The Germany Under-21 international has scored 14 goals and provided one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions this season, establishing himself as one of the most productive young forwards on the continent.

His form has inevitably generated transfer speculation, with reports suggesting that Bayern view him as a potential long-term addition to their attacking department.

Significantly, the club's interest emerged before Kane suffered his injury against Koln.

Earlier this month, Bayern were reportedly exploring the possibility of signing Tresoldi as an additional attacking option despite having recently extended Kane's contract until 2029. The idea was to strengthen their squad with a younger centre-forward capable of developing alongside the England international.

That strategy could now face an unexpected test.

With Kane unavailable for several months, Bayern must decide whether their existing attacking resources can compensate for his absence or whether an immediate signing would provide greater security.

Tresoldi possesses several attributes that could appeal to Kompany, including his movement inside the penalty area, ability to attack space behind defenders and increasingly reliable finishing.

However, securing his signature midway through the campaign would be far from straightforward.

Reports in Belgium have indicated that Club Brugge are determined to retain the striker until at least the summer, with the club's hierarchy reluctant to entertain offers during the January transfer window.

According to Het Nieuwsblad, Brugge have made their position clear to interested clubs, although an exceptional financial proposal could potentially force a reassessment.

German reports have placed Tresoldi's potential price between €40m (£35m) and €50m (£44m), with the forward under contract until June 2029.

Bayern have not submitted a confirmed offer, and there is currently no evidence that Kane's injury has prompted formal negotiations with the Belgian club.

Any attempt to accelerate a move for Tresoldi could also bring Bayern into competition with several Premier League clubs.

Arsenal and Manchester United have both been linked with the Club Brugge striker, whose impressive scoring record has strengthened his reputation as one of Europe's most promising young centre-forwards.

That timeline broadly aligned with Bayern's previous interest, which appeared to concern the longer-term development of their attacking squad rather than an urgent winter acquisition.

Kane's injury introduces a potentially important difference in Bayern's circumstances, although it does not establish that the Bundesliga champions have changed their transfer strategy.

The club must also assess whether investing heavily in another centre-forward would make sense once Kane returns to fitness, particularly after committing to a new long-term agreement with their leading goalscorer.

Kompany has alternatives within his squad, but none offers the same combination of finishing, creativity and experience as the England captain.

A temporary tactical adjustment may therefore be necessary, with greater responsibility potentially falling on Bayern's other attacking players.

The German champions could also turn to their academy, where 16-year-old Bastian Assomo has attracted attention following impressive performances for the youth teams.

According to Kicker, the teenager was already under consideration for greater involvement with the senior squad before Kane's injury, although expecting him to replace the England international immediately would represent a considerable leap.

For Bayern, the dilemma is therefore as much about timing as identifying the right player.

Tresoldi was already an attractive prospect before Kane's setback, but Brugge's reported resistance to a January sale means that accelerating the deal could prove expensive and difficult.

Meanwhile, Arsenal and Manchester United remain interested parties whose own plans have been linked to the summer window.

Bayern's next decision will depend on whether Kompany believes his squad can absorb Kane's absence or whether the club considers an early investment necessary to protect its ambitions in the Bundesliga and Champions League.

#1934. Sheffield Wednesday fans can see the light, Barnsley FC just look lost

Three words from the 5,700 Sheffield Wednesday supporters at Oakwell carried so much meaning – especially with Barnsley wandering around looking lost.

The football fans who turn up on freezing cold nights like Friday's and pay to watch a match they could just as easily see from their sofa or a warm pub indisputably love their clubs, but do not always feeling in tune with them.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Barnsley's appreciated the efforts of their players in a frustrating 2-1 loss and understand the handicaps their coach, Daniel Stendel, is fighting against. But their dissatisfaction with the direction those above are taking the club in was vented outside the ground before kick-off.

They cannot see how their club can get back to where they want it to be without a big change of direction.

The same was true of Wednesday's fans a year ago as they emerged from the wreckage wrought by Dejphon Chansiri. Although David Storch's takeover brought optimism they were not convinced manager Henrik Pedersen was going in quite the right direction.

His successor, Dave Challinor, is miles from his destination but even if it might have been premature after two league games, "Wednesday are back" was a vote of confidence he can guide them to the right path.

The Owls did not play at anywhere near the level of the team they aspire to be. Jamal Lowe's goals were their only shots on target.

Much has been made of the entertainment levels this season, but a night so cold you could see every breath in a derby mismatched enough that you felt the Owls had much more to lose than gain was not about putting on a show, just coming back into the warm three points better off.

Barry Bannan ran around like a man ten years younger, Liam Cooper marshalled his defence, Lowe played in a wide position that demands a lot of dirty work without forgetting his primary job.

Barnsley refused to accept their fate when Lowe scored his second goal after 14 minutes.

The trouble is, like Wednesday's players last season, they are just not good enough for the level. Between the boxes they are, but not the bits that decide matches.

Their defending for Lowe's goals – leaving Cooper unmarked at a Bannan corner to head across to Lowe, then standing off the striker as he finished a move which took them from the halfway line to the back of the net in two passes and a shot – was relegation standard.

With the exception of Vimal Yoganathan arriving onto Reyes Cleary's low ball in to halve the deficit after 40 minutes, their final balls and finishes were not much better.

That they are trying their best only highlights their best is not good enough – not by much in most games, but by enough in almost all of them. Their winless run in League One now stretches to double figures – unlike their points tally.

Bromley's win at Reading on Saturday sent them bottom of the table.

It is hard to see them escaping relegation without a really good January transfer window, and very hard to imagine even a quite good one.

"When you play games like Sheffield or Stockport or Oxford. Luton, you do not have the feeling the gap is too so big," said Stendel after 90 minutes which backed him up.

"Between both boxes, we are surely a team who shouldn't be in the bottom of the league, but games decided not between the boxes.

"You would think, 'What you do in training?' but (on Thursday) we prepared the team especially for a situation like (the second goal)."

Whilst adamant his team can pull things around, Patrick Kelly – standing in for the suspended Cameron McGeehan as captain – was not pulling any punches.

"You can't start games like that," he said. "We just had too many times this season where we just gave ourselves too much to do.

"We've conceded far too many from free-kicks and stuff.

"After that we were good, probably the better team for the rest of the game, but didn't create enough clear-cut chances."

Barnsley's doom and gloom was in contrast to the joy of away fans who made up about a third of the crowd condensed into one end.

It felt important they shared it with the players at full-time.

"They have to enjoy it and look forward to the next one," said Challinor. "It's probably a little bit outside my comfort zone (celebrating).

"It's brilliant to be able to celebrate, but more brilliant to be able to send them home happy. They've been through the mill over the past couple of years, and maybe there's a little bit of a feeling they've got the they've got the football club back.

"You build that camaraderie between the team and supporters by winning and we've done that on the last couple of couple of occasions.

"We need to improve individually, collectively. There's so much more to come.

"But most importantly for the supporters, they want to see effort. They want to see the team put the bodies on the line. They did that in the second half."

After too much darkness, they think they can see the light. Barnsley fans are squinting to make it out.

That looked to be that, only for Rovers defender Sean Grehan to head home a dramatic leveller in the fifth minute of stoppage time in a 2-2 draw.

Duff said: "We were having an argument because they were saying he (Morgan) punched him (Broadbent) and he hasn't at all.

"They've had a little wrestle and thrown him to the ground a little bit - that's where me and Grant had a chat about it.

"It's something and nothing. I've been doing that with Grant for 30 years. We used to have arguments on PlayStation games, when we were 20 years old and who's going to walk the dog? And we'd kick lumps out of each other in training.

"So that's just two blokes who want to win. I think that's why we're still in a job. We're both nearly 50 years old.

"You look back, it's pathetic, really. But in the moment, it's... I don't get who that person is at any one moment in time. It could be my missus.

"If she doesn't want me to win, then I'm against her. And then it was literally nothing. There was a disagreement in terms of the incident.

"They thought he punched him. I knew he hadn't. That's all it was."

McCann added: "I don't know what happened.

"I watched it back. I think it was a coming together in the box and then Morgan retaliated to George.

"To be honest, when I watch the back, it's probably the right decision from Darren Drysdale. I don't think there was anything in it. "Michael was just in my technical area and I just said 'get out of it', that was it.

"He should know better not to be in my area or else he'll get kicked out of it.

"He was talking about the incident, but I'd not seen the incident.

"They talk to me about iPads and Bradford, but Michael watched his iPad before I had an idea."

Asked if he would have a post-match beer with Duff, he said: "Absolutely.. If he lets me in..."

#1930. Bradford City 2 Doncaster Rovers 2: Untidiness at home resurfaces for Michael Duff as good mate Grant McCann has last laugh

"The untidiest man I have ever lived with in my life" was his pre-match assertion ahead of Saturday's reunion with his old housemate.

As a manager, Duff could not be more different. The Bradford City chief - a businesslike defender back in the day - prides himself on order and neatness.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

His early days in his new workplace have reinforced that. City kept five clean sheets in his first five matches in charge and in all competitions, they recorded seven in his opening eight games.

In the club's last two league games at Valley Parade, derbies against Huddersfield Town and McCann's Doncaster Rovers, there has been some disorder at home again.

After letting in three goals in uncharacteristic fashion against Town, City's famed defence was opened up twice in Saturday's final quarter.

The first, like Town's opener, was a majestic overhead kick which you have to doff your cap to - Jordan Thomas, take a bow. The second, in the fifth minute of stoppage time, was a different matter as Rovers helped themselves to a second equaliser in a finale which was as lively as the opening hour was eminently forgettable.

Unmarked Sean Grehan, who had an eventful second half, benefited from City's inattentiveness following Robbie Gotts' corner. It was an untidy concession, but a precious moment for Rovers, given recent events on the road.

McCann’s side needed a spark. The game definitely got one when George Broadbent clashed with Bantams rival Kieran Morgan in the second half, the prelude to a brief melee among players and kerfuffle between both benches. The crowd got involved and it became a proper derby.

Duff, cautioned alongside McCann, remarked: "I've been doing that with Grant for 30 years. We used to have arguments on PlayStation games, when we were 20 years old and who's going to walk the dog? And we'd kick lumps out of each other in training.

"So that's just two blokes who want to win. I think that's why we're still in a job. We're both nearly 50 years old. You look back, it's pathetic, really."

In the red corner, McCann added: "Michael was just in my technical area and I just said 'Get out of it', that was it.

"He should know better than to be in my area or else he'll get kicked out of it.."

If any of the ex-video game enthusiasts had a grumble at the result, it was Duff. It wasn’t on a Grand Theft Auto scale, but it was a mini heist.

City were in prime position to win the game twice but allowed Rovers to score from two efforts on target. Very un-Bradford-like.

The fact that two strikers scored for the hosts at least provided further evidence to dispel the notion that City don’t have enough goals in them.

Nick Powell - whose minutes must be strictly monitored - was entering the red zone when he struck in the 55th minute.

It was a classic centre forward’s header after getting in between Grehan and Tom Nixon following Callum Connolly’s superb cross.

It was the first defensive blemish on the day for Rovers, as disciplined at Bradford as they were dishevelled at Kidderminster and MK Dons.

A magnificent save from Tommy Simkin kept out a header from Powell’s replacement Stephen Humphrys. A ‘big turning point’ said Duff. It was the cue for Thomas to come to the party.

A low shot flew inches wide before a volley hit the woodwork. It was a case of third time lucky when he splendidly levelled in sublime fashion after debutant James Collins expertly cushioned a header into his path following Grehan’s deep centre.

Making his long-awaited bow, Collins' canny, authoritative performance after coming on midway through the second half whet the appetite.

Play then swung back to the Kop with Will Swan picking out Humphrys after Rovers were caught cold from Jon McCracken’s punt forward. His drilled finish was unerring.

More Simkin heroics then thwarted Humphrys. Rovers dug deep and got their precious reward.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) writes that the Milan squad will return to full strength with the arrival of the final players returning from international duty, allowing Ruben Amorim to begin detailed preparations for Sunday’s 18:00 CET clash against Frosinone at San Siro.

Mike Maignan is expected to start in goal. He took part in a portion of yesterday’s training session alongside the other goalkeepers. The Frenchman’s recovery is progressing well, and Pietro Terracciano – who has been out for about 40 days with a shoulder issue – could make the bench.

#1925. Jeglertz not worried despite Man City’s ‘wake-up call’ loss to Spurs

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Andree Jeglertz wants Manchester City to use their loss to Tottenham as a "wake-up call" as they missed the chance to go top of the Women's Super League.

Spurs stunned City at home, coming from behind to beat the reigning champions 3-1 and deal Jeglertz his first home league loss in charge of the club.

City started well, with Khadija Shaw breaking the deadlock just 10 minutes in. Matilda Vinberg was caught in possession, and Jade Rose set up the Jamaican for her 16th WSL goal against Spurs.

But the visitors responded well, with Cathinka Tandberg drawing them level five minutes before the break, and City offered little in their attempts to regain their lead after the break.

But with 16 minutes to play, Vinberg – who was a last-minute replacement after Olivia Holdt was taken ill – put Spurs in front before she then teed up substitute Jessica Naz for the insurance goal five minutes later.

City have failed to win a WSL home game under Jeglertz for the first time, ending the second-longest winning streak on home turf in the competition (17 in a row).

Despite the loss, Jeglertz is not too concerned about the result as he feels he will get a strong response from his side.

"We want more, and I think no matter what, we're such a good team with great players that we need more from each other," Jeglertz said.

"Sometimes it's not your day, but sometimes also, it's almost a wake-up call. We know this league is tough, and we won’t take anything for granted.

"If you don't have a good day, the opponent will punish you, which I think they did. We just need to deal with that in a good way and then move on from it.

"It's always going to be like that; it's a tough league. It'll be a long race, so we need to deal with it in a good way and come back. I'm not worried about that."

A win would have taken City above Chelsea, who dropped points against Liverpool on Saturday, but they remain two points behind the league leaders.

Their city rivals Manchester United close in on the top three, though, with a dramatic 2-1 win over Birmingham City.

Having gone 1-0 down inside four minutes thanks to Lee Geum-Min's goal, United rallied with a late comeback, with Simi Awujo netting a 94th-minute winner after Elisabeth Terland had equalised.

Arsenal's struggles at the Emirates continued, however, as they remain without a league win on home soil this term after a 0-0 draw with West Ham.
