#1923. Pep Guardiola visits Bahia in new City Football Group role

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 11:00

Pep Guardiola has made his first visit to Brazilian club Bahia, offering a glimpse into his continuing involvement with Manchester City's global football network several months after leaving his managerial position at the Etihad Stadium.

The former Man City manager arrived in Salvador this week alongside Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group (CFG), which has controlled 90% of Bahia's football operations since 2023. The trip forms part of Guardiola's responsibilities as a global ambassador for the organisation, a position he assumed following his departure from the Premier League club in May.

Guardiola visited Bahia's Cidade Tricolor training complex on Friday, November 20, where he was welcomed by head coach Rogério Ceni and given a tour of the facilities. The 55-year-old also watched a training session ahead of Saturday's Brazilian Serie A encounter with Coritiba, which he is scheduled to attend at the Arena Fonte Nova.

The visit marks a significant moment in Guardiola's relationship with Bahia, a club he first publicly embraced before its integration into City Football Group was completed. Although he is no longer responsible for Manchester City's first team, his presence in Brazil illustrates how the organisation continues to involve its former manager in activities across its international network.

Guardiola's interest in Bahia dates back to 2022, when the club were attempting to secure promotion from Brazil's second division. Before a decisive fixture, he recorded a video message wishing the players success, alongside contributions from other Manchester City representatives.

The relationship developed further after Bahia's supporters approved the club's proposed partnership with CFG in December 2022. The agreement was subsequently completed in May 2023, giving the group a controlling stake in one of Brazil's best-supported clubs.

Speaking in January 2023, Guardiola welcomed the arrangement and expressed his desire to visit Salvador.

"I'm delighted to know that we're together with them. It was a democratic vote by the supporters, and more than 90% wanted it," he said at the time. "Now invite me so that one day I can go to Brazil, to Bahia, to see them."

Almost four years later, that invitation has finally been fulfilled. Guardiola's reunion with Ceni on Friday also continued a relationship established when Bahia visited Manchester for pre-season preparations.

During their earlier meeting, Guardiola praised the former Brazilian goalkeeper, describing him as a "legend" and highlighting his remarkable goalscoring record. Ceni, who scored more than 100 goals during his playing career, has since remained in charge of Bahia as the club attempts to establish itself among Brazil's leading sides.

The Brazilian coach was equally complimentary ahead of Guardiola's arrival, describing the Spaniard as someone who had changed the way football is played.

"It's a pleasure, not just for me but for everyone," Ceni told reporters. "I hope we can produce a performance worthy of having someone of his calibre watching us."

Guardiola ended his decade-long spell as Manchester City manager at the conclusion of the 2025-26 campaign, closing one of the most successful managerial eras in English football. However, leaving the dugout did not bring his association with City's ownership structure to an end.

As a global ambassador, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach maintains an institutional connection with CFG, whose portfolio includes clubs such as Girona in Spain, New York City FC in the United States and Montevideo City Torque in Uruguay.

His journey to Brazil has also included corporate engagements in São Paulo alongside Soriano, before the pair travelled to Salvador for activities associated with Bahia. Their itinerary included the launch of a documentary, O Bahia é o Mundo – A Era City, exploring the Brazilian club's relationship with its international ownership group.

The visit should not be interpreted as evidence that Guardiola has assumed a formal coaching or recruitment role at Bahia. No such responsibilities have been announced, and the activities confirmed during his trip are consistent with his ambassadorial position.

Nevertheless, his presence alongside CFG's chief executive demonstrates that Guardiola remains a prominent representative of the organisation beyond his achievements in Manchester. For Bahia, it also provides an opportunity to showcase the club and its facilities to one of the most recognisable figures in world football.

Attention now turns to Saturday's meeting with Coritiba, where Guardiola is expected to watch from the stands as Bahia pursue qualification for next season's Copa Libertadores.

Ceni's team entered the weekend sixth in the Brazilian top flight with 53 points, occupying a position that would currently secure a place in the competition's preliminary rounds.

For Guardiola, the occasion will complete a journey he first discussed publicly in 2023, when he asked Bahia supporters to invite him to Brazil. This time, he will be watching their team in person rather than following its progress from Manchester.

#1922. How Leeds United disrupted a Premier League narrative with historic win over Chelsea - analysis

‘Get your passports out for Daniel Farke’ was the song of choice as Leeds United dismantled Chelsea in their own backyard, roaring to a 4-1 victory.

Admittedly there was an expletive in that chant to strengthen the sense of enthusiasm, as well as the belief Leeds are ascending to new levels.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Not since December 2002 have Leeds fulfilled a European fixture. Then again, they had not beaten Chelsea at Stamford Bridge since 1999 before they turned up and ran riot. Streaks are there to be ended.

Leeds boss Farke has made a conscious effort to dampen talk of planes and passports, not to spoil the mood but to manage the expectations of an intense fanbase.

By leading his side to a such a convincing victory over a team of expensive global stars, he did not help his campaign of pressure control.

“If you face a side who has world-class potential and world-class potential players, if you dominate the side, then you could label yourself to be more or less from the first to the last second of the game, the better team, it gives lots of belief and lots of confidence,” said Farke. “Yes, of course, it's always good for the mood.

“But it is even more important also for the table to add three more important points, so it's important during this period of the season to collect points in order to make sure that you finish in the right position.

“It will definitely give us more confidence, but to be honest, we also travelled here with confidence and belief, otherwise it wouldn't be possible to show such a dominant performance.”

Chelsea drew first blood on the 25-minute mark, when the imposing Emmanuel Emegha rifled a shot past James Trafford at the goalkeeper’s near post.

Noah Okafor cancelled out the opener three minutes later - and from there Leeds only grew in confidence. The Swiss winger was to strike again, adding a third after Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s penalty had put the Whites ahead.

By the time Brenden Aaronson weighed in with a fourth from the bench, the party in the away end was well underway.

There is a common narrative when Leeds - or others who threaten the established elites in the Premier League’s upper echelons - gatecrash the top eight.

Pundits and fans have a tendency to focus upon physicality and intensity, sometimes discarding technical and tactical qualities to paint a picture of athletic brutes.

Leeds’ players undoubtedly have robust engines - and they certainly have aggression - but Chelsea were outwitted just as much as they were outfought.

“We looked very, very dominant today in our pressing and with our intensity,” said Farke. “We always had pressure on the ball, but it has more to do with a tactical plan and a tactical solution and how you want to be good against the ball, how you structure your team and also how you want to bypass the opponent than really just fitness level, because on this level all the boys are fit and outstanding.

“If it would be just about physical strength, I would go into the gym and get some bodybuilders and set them on the pitch.”

There is a widespread acceptance of Farke’s reluctance to discuss Leeds’ potential ceiling - and he is of course right not to get carried away. Leeds are just 11 games in and there will almost certainly be weeks in which they face criticism before the curtain comes down on the 2026/27 campaign.

The music that boomed out of the Leeds dressing room was not quite to Farke’s taste, but he knew better than to pretend it was not fun to bask in the glow of a remarkable afternoon.

“For me it's a bit too loud,” he said. “I'm a bit too old for this.

“But I'm not dead yet, so sometimes I can also enjoy it a little bit after a game like this. They fully deserve to celebrate themselves. I still remember my time, so after a game like this you would enjoy the night and go out and celebrate and also fully deserve.

“At my age right now, you're looking forward to heading home as soon as possible and I can enjoy a little bit of time on the sofa with coffee and cake.”

There is not a patisserie in Leeds that would not clear their shelves for Farke after that display.

Unused substitutes: Zetterer, Bijol, James, Nmecha.

#1918. Konstantinos Tzolakis kept Hull City 'alive' to pull off famous win, says Sergej Jakirovic

The Tigers welcomed in-form Brighton and Hove Albion, and beat them 2-0 with goals from Oli McBurnie in stoppage time.

That did not tell the whole story, with Brighton the dominant side for much of the game, only to be denied by another brilliant performance from Hull goalkeeper Tzolakis. The Seagulls also hit the woodwork, though in fairness so too did Hull.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The combination of defensive brilliance and clinical finishing on the counter-attack made, in Jakirovic's words, for a "good recipe”.

"We played against an excellent team," he said. "They're playing very intensive football. A lot of movement.

"Some moments of the game, I couldn't track them on the pitch.

"But congratulations to our lads, they gave everything. We had problems with injuries, with cramps.

"We survived the first half because Tzolakis was amazing there. I thought a few balls were in the net, to be honest. But this is his quality.

"We are very happy because of these three points, especially a victory after almost three months, which is excellent.

"I feel very good. I wish this feeling would never stop.

"I know how demanding it is and you see every week and every game, it's very difficult.

"Everyone fights there for the points, but it will be very big confidence for us and a big boost for the next game."

Jakirovic acknowledged the part Tzolkais played in keeping his team in the game until the coach could make some decisive substitutions.

"Because of him we were still alive," he said. "It could be two, 3-0 and then finish the game, ciao.

"With Sorba (Thomas, who hit the crossbar), with (Lucas) Gourna (who set up the first goal), with (Elliot) Stroud and after (that Ryan) Giles, especially on the left side, we had much more stability. Jens (Hjerto-Dahl) also gave us a lot of stability, a lot of energy."

Brighton opened the door to Hull by having Joao Costinha sent off for two fouls on Thomas, the second in the 89th minute.

"After this red card, I want to take more risks," said Jakirovic. "We scored two goals from counter-attacks, but I think this first goal, they played brilliantly, very precise.

"(Regan) Slater to Jens, Jens to Slater, to Gourna, and then Oli McBurnie.

"That was a very good signing, because it's about age, it's about his experience, he's young goalkeeper but very experienced, and an international. He had difficult times now in the last international break (when Greece lost 7-0 in the Netherlands), but this is not his fault.

"Okay, maybe he could stop some goals (this season), but also he could concede some goals, so he's doing very well and I hope he will continue like this."

The biggest negative was that midfielder Tim Iroegbunam went off injured at the end of a strong first half for him.

"I was thinking it's knee, it doesn't look good, but he said to me now that he has a problem with his hamstring," said Jakirovic. "We will see."

By Oliver Thomas | 21 Nov 2026 11:18, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 11:35

Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki have both been left out of Manchester City’s starting lineup for this afternoon’s Premier League fixture against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium.

The Citizens are seeking to bounce back from a run of three successive top-flight defeats, most recently losing 3-1 away against Nottingham Forest before the international break.

Manager Enzo Maresca has made a total of three changes to the side that were beaten at the City Ground, with Fernandez, Cherki and Josko Gvardiol all dropping down to the substitutes’ bench.

While Cherki scored in the defeat to Forest, Gvardiol was at fault for a first-half goal conceded by City and Fernandez’s position in midfield has come under question in recent weeks.

Ayyoub Bouaddi will start just his third Premier League game at the expense of Fernandez, while Phil Foden and Nico O'Reilly have been brought in for Cherki and Gvardiol respectively.

While Matheus Nunes missed out through injury, Abdukodir Khusanov has shaken off a knock to start at right-back, joining O'Reilly, Marc Guehi and Ruben Dias in a four-man defence protecting goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Bouaddi will links arms with Elliot Anderson in centre-midfield, with Foden set to operate in the number 10 role between wingers Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku.

Leading the line is goal machine Erling Haaland, who has scored eight goals in as many games against Fulham and is looking to net his 10th Premier League goal of the campaign this afternoon.

As for Fulham, head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has also made a total of three changes to the team that rescued a 1-1 draw with Newcastle United a fortnight ago.

The headline alteration see Gonzalo Garcia begin as a substitute for the first time since joining the Cottagers in the summer following a run of nine straight starts without a goal.

Rodrigo Muniz, who scored a late equaliser off the bench against Newcastle, has been rewarded with his first league start of the campaign at Garcia’s expense.

Arbeloa has also opted to change his full-backs, with Kenny Tete and Ryan Sessegnon coming in for Timothy Castagne and Antonee Robinson. Calvin Bassey and David Affengruber retain their places at centre-back, though.

Man City academy graduates Shea Charles and Oscar Bobb both start against their former club, with the former to play alongside Sander Berge in midfield and the latter continuing on the right flank.

Manchester City starting lineup: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly; Bouaddi, Anderson; Ndiaye, Foden, Doku; Haaland

Subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Cherki, Fernandez, Reis, Gvardiol, Allan, F. Samba, Lewis

Fulham starting lineup: Leno; Tete, Affengruber, Bassey, Sessegnon; Berge, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Muniz

Subs: Kaiser, Castagne, Cuenca, Robinson, Larsson, Cairney, Angel, Palacios, Garcia

#1915. ‘They had faith’ – Moyes reflects on Everton legacy ahead of milestone match

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

David Moyes credited Everton with giving him his first big break in management as he prepares to oversee a record-breaking 593rd match in charge of the club.

Moyes is set to surpass Harry Catterick's record of 592 games managed as Everton boss when his side make the trip to face Brentford in the Premier League.

He first made the move to Merseyside in 2002 from Preston North End and remained in the Everton dugout for 11 years before replacing Alex Ferguson at Manchester United.

The 63-year-old went on to have spells at Real Sociedad, Sunderland and West Ham before returning to Everton in January 2025 to replace Sean Dyche.

During his two stints with the Toffees, Moyes has overseen 250 wins in all competitions (D155 L187), and his Everton side have started the 2026-27 campaign brightly.

Everton are seventh after signing off for the international break with a win over Coventry City, and Moyes wants that upward trajectory to continue in his milestone match.

"I'm really thrilled about it, but if I'm honest, it's not something I really think about," Moyes told reporters ahead of the trip to the Gtech Community Stadium.

"I've suddenly become the manager who has managed more Everton games than anyone before. That's a privilege and an honour to be put in that position.

"I have to thank the people who brought me to the club. When you take a chance on a young manager, you never know if it'll work, but they had faith and believed in me.

"I'm so thankful for the people around Everton because they've been so good for me."

A presentation from Blues past and present. Leon Osman and James Tarkowski surprise David Moyes with a memento as he sets a new record for games managed for Everton Football Club (593). https://t.co/tzFuGeUhFW

Brentford boss Keith Andrews paid respect to the Scot.

"I played against his Everton team. I've always had a lot of respect for him, even when I was a player," Andrews said of the Everton boss.

"He's now an iconic manager of English football, with how long he's been involved and how successful he's been."

Brentford know a win will see them leapfrog Everton in the Premier League, but they must do so without Igor Thiago, who was sent off against Brighton last time out.

Thiago was shown a red card for violent conduct in an incident with Chema Andres after a VAR review, with an appeal against the decision unanimously rejected.

Put to him that Callum Wilson could come in as a direct replacement in attack, Andrews added: "That would be your natural thinking.

"We've got three players that have played that position and can play that position; wide players could become more central options. We have Fabio Carvalho coming back as well.

"There are different ways that we can play, but Callum has obviously been champing at the bit. I do not doubt that he is going to get a decent number of minutes."

With Thiago suspended, Andrews looks set to name Wilson as his starting striker against Everton, and it is not a bad replacement to have.

Wilson has failed to score in the Premier League this season, but he does have a good record against Everton. Only against West Ham (12) has he scored more top-flight goals against than the Toffees (nine).

Barry's six goals are the most by a player in Everton's first 10 Premier League games of a season since Dominic Calvert-Lewin in 2020-21 (10), and the most by a non-English player for the club since Romelu Lukaku in 2016-17 (seven).

The Frenchman has scored (five) or assisted (one) six of the Toffees' last seven league goals, and you feel he will be key to his side's chances of victory here.

With 13 goal involvements from his first 13 matches of the 2026-27 season (10 goals, 3 assists), Thierno Barry looks like a man on a mission @jord_coll sat down exclusively with Everton striker to discuss his sensational start to the season, and how training with a former club legend has helped take him to new heights https://t.co/xZG7SZHbcO

— Opta Analyst (@OptaAnalyst) November 20, 2026

Having won their first Premier League home game against Everton 1-0 in November 2021, Brentford are winless in their last four against them at the Gtech (D3 L1).

Andrews' side have, however, won four of their last seven Premier League games at the Gtech (D2 L1), and are looking for back-to-back home league wins for the first time in 2026, having last done so in November 2025 (three in a row).

But the Bees have won just one of their last 11 Premier League games that have come the matchday following an international break (D5 L5) – although that was the only such match they played on a Monday in this period, beating West Ham 2-0 in October 2025.

Everton, meanwhile, have lost just one of their last eight Premier League games against Brentford (W3 D4), though they are winless in their last four against them (D3 L1).

This will be Everton's ninth top-flight game played on a Monday since the start of last season, three more than any other side in this time (Manchester United six). The Toffees have lost just one of their last seven on this day of the week (W2 D4), winning their last two away from home.

Moyes' men have won back-to-back Premier League games for the first time since between February and March, and are looking to win three in a row in the competition for the first time since May 2025.

#1914. Ian Wright orders Arsenal to buy £67m star in January following Newcastle draw

Ian Wright has urged Arsenal to go out and buy Antonio Nusa from RB Leipzig in the January transfer window.

Despite a 2-2 draw with Newcastle United on Saturday night, the Gunners remain six points clear at the summit of the Premier League and are still firm favourites to defend their crown.

But their limitations in attack were again exposed on Tyneside. Eberechi Eze opened the scoring on the night with Noni Madueke impressing on the right with Bukayo Saka out injured but the visitors were short on inspiration off the bench.

Christos Tzolis came on in the second-half for a forgettable cameo with Viktor Gyokeres labouring once again after his introduction.

Arsenal explored deals to sign Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr in the summer but Tzolis was their sole addition in attack once the window closed with Gabriel Martinelli and Leonardo Trossard also moving on.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Arsenal are interested in signing RB Leipzig star Nusa who is enjoying a superb season with the German club, with seven goals and eight assists in 16 appearances.

Leipzig have put a huge €80million (£67m) price tag on the Norway international who operates on the left for club and country.

While convinced Arsenal are well stocked in all other areas, club legend Wright believes Nusa could offer a much-improved option in attack and also raise the game of Kai Havertz.

‘I’d want to go [and strengthen] on the left side and up front. At some stage we have got to say “we have got to go for it.”

‘We have been linked with Nusa at RB Leipzig. If think we should just go and get him,’ Wright told Sky Sports.

‘We saw today with Tzolis, I didn’t see enough.

‘I think with Havertz, if he’s got someone at the same level or better and push him I think we get more out of him which he needs and I don’t think that’s happening through Gyokeres.’

#1913. Hull City 2 Brighton and Hove Albion 0: Konstantinos Tzolakis and Tiger spirit seal huge win

Not for the first time, they were outplayed and won. This is a squad made of tough stuff.

"Ballsy” was the new English word Sergej Jakirovic learnt in his post-match press conference, and it sums up his players. They are not afraid to have less of the ball than their opponents, and when Brighton and Hove Albion opened the door to them with a stupid second yellow card for Joao Costinha, they were brave enough to try and go through it.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

For a most of Sunday's game it looked like hanging on for a draw against outstanding opponents might be the best Hull could hope for and thanks to the brilliance of goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, that was a real possibility.

But two counter-attack goals from Oli McBurnie saw them to a first Premier League win since August.

If there was much to marvel at in Brighton's football, the same could be said for the Tigers' mentality.

Brilliantly coached, stable and with a clear method that means everyone knows their job and that of the players around them, the Seagulls are a class act, and it was no surprise they put Hull under real pressure in the first half in particular.

But they do not have the monopoly on shrewd signings, and Tzolakis – plus a bit of luck – kept them at bay until McBurnie was ready to make his decisive late contribution,

Having changed formation to a 4-2-3-1, Hull started with good intent, McBurnie winning the ball in the final third inside two minutes, but left winger Mohamed-Ali Cho shot wide from a tight angle.

When Cho robbed Lewis Dunk, it was McBurnie unable to score.

Kept in the side after Matt Crooks’ recall, French youth international Cho did not have a great day, criticised by his manager for not working hard enough defensively and substituted at half-time.

As the game went on, Brighton turned the screw and really should have scored before the break.

Tzolakis, signed from Olympiacos for £20m, was called upon to make his first top save in the 15th minute as Brighton began to move the ball around with speed and accuracy.

Diego Gomez arrived onto a ball in from Maxim de Cuyper, but found the goalkeeper in the way.

Minutes later Nobel Mendy had to charge down a shot from former Leeds United striker Georginio Rutter. When a 20th-minute free-kick was headed back from far too much space at the far post, Costinha really ought to have hit the target.

Semi Ajayi was pressed into giving the ball up quickly after, but left-back Elliot Stroud got a boot on Gomez's shot to deflect it wide.

Tzolakis saved a Rutter shot with his feet, although had he not, the video assistant referee might well have been checking for an offside.

Yasin Ayari hit the frame of the goal after 37 minutes and when Rutter pounced on the rebound, Tzolakis’ left hand denied him.

Until an audacious flick from Crooks forced Bart Verbruggen to save, Hull only hinted at moments on the counter-attack. Mohamed Belloumi had Verbruggen down to a low free-kick in the 40th minute.

Gomez missed the best chance of the half at the end of it when an Olivier Boscagli went all the way through to him at the far post but he dragged his shot beyond the near.

That came after Gomez picked Pascal Gross out in far too much space in the inside-right pocket, and he turned and force another save.

Tzolakis also saved from Dunk when Mendy's headed clearance picked him out, but the centre-back's shot lacked the power to trouble a goalkeeper in such good form.

Brighton were never quite the same force after the break, the question increasingly became whether Hull could find a ruthless moment on the counter-attack.

Belloumi came inside in the 50th minute but Verbruggen got down well again, then when Regan Slater brilliantly released the winger, his shot rippled the outside of the net.

A minute later half-time substitute Sorba Thomas looked to have lost the ball as he stumbled, but recovered only to mishit his cross. It kissed the crossbar.

Slater ought to have made the decisive mistake in the 79th minute when his poor pass picked out Charalampos Kostoulas but got back to brilliantly head the shot dinked over Tzolakis off the line.

Thomas was a real menace, and Costinha was sent off for fouling him in the 63rd and 89th minute.

Slater's measured pass to Lucas Gourna was gorgeous and although it looked like McBurnie had made a mess of it, Hull do not give up easily and the striker forced it home.

His next goal, as Hull broke down the right again, was more routine, Belloumi squaring to him in space for a simple tap-in.

Hull City: Tzolakis; Coyle (Norton-Cuffy 84), Ajayi, Mendy, Stroud (Giles 66); Iroegbunam (Gourna 45) Slater; Belloumi, Crooks (Hjerto-Dahl 66), Cho (Thomas HT); McBurnie. Unused substitutes: Butland, Egan, Herrington, Vaz.

Brighton and Hove Albion: Verbruggen; Costinha, Vuskovic, Dunk, Boscagli (Minteh 66); Gross, Andres (Osman 90+3); Gomez (Kadıoglu 80), Ayari (Hinshelwood 66), Thomas, de Cuyper; Rutter (Kostoulas 66). Unused substitutes: Steele, Wieffer, Svoboda, O'Riley.

​Super subs: Sergej Jakirovic’s substitutions made the difference for Hull. Tim Iroegbunam’s first-half injury was a blow, but Lucas Gourna and Jens Hjerto-Dahl played a big part in the all-important first goal, and Sorba Thomas was a constant pest when he came on on the left.

Greek hero: Konstanintos Tzolakis has been an outstanding signing since joining from Olympiacos in the summer. With James Trafford joining Leeds United in the same window, Yorkshire now boasts two of the Premier League’s best goalkeepers.

Random complaint: With three holidays given away at half-time, there was much grumbling from three signs of the ground when all three seats randomly picked out to win them were in the North Stand.

#1912. Roberto De Zerbi speaks out on ‘unlucky’ Savio injury in Tottenham’s Ipswich win

Tottenham winger Savio returned from injury on Saturday and almost immediately suffered the same injury that had just kept him out for six weeks.

Spurs beat Ipswich Town 2-0 in north London, thanks to goals from teenager Luca Williams-Barnett on his first Premier League start and Dominic Solanke.

Tottenham climbed to ninth with the win, but there was disappointing news for them as Savio came off the bench in the second half but did not make the final whistle.

The summer-signing from Manchester City had not played since the draw with Manchester United on October 10 and may now face a similar period on the sidelines after a recurrence of the same hamstring problem.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi said: ‘I’m sorry for Savio’s injury, because it was the same injury as last time, and we need him.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘He’s a crucial player for us. He’s unlucky in this period. We have to be close with him to help him to become the top player we bought at the beginning of this season.’

The 22-year-old joined from Manchester City for an initial £75 million and scored on his debut in a League Cup win over Charlton Athletic, but has not done much of note since then, hampered by injury.

The emergence of Williams-Barnett is much better news for De Zerbi, who has not been shy in talking up the talents of the 18-year-old who has come through the youth ranks at Spurs.

‘Luca is a special player,’ said the Italian. ‘I’m not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He’s lucky because he’s playing in a top club with top team-mates.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important.

‘The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

‘And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

‘Even if they are Ballon d’Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch.’

De Zerbi, who was serving a touchline suspension against Ipswich, was asked if Williams-Barnett could reach the levels of the superstars he mentioned and said: ‘Yes, I think so.

‘And one of the best things in my career… I’ve seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

‘I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?’

Spurs have now won four of their last five Premier League games and ended Saturday just three points adrift of Bournemouth in fourth.

#1911. Brentford predicted lineup vs. Everton: Igor Thiago replacement decided for Premier League clash

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 11:23, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 11:34

Brentford striker Igor Thiago begins a three-match suspension in Monday's Premier League battle with Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Thiago was sent off for violent conduct in the Bees' 2-0 loss to Brighton & Hove Albion before the international break, and Brentford have since failed with an appeal.

Thiago will therefore miss Monday's match and upcoming battles with Manchester United and Arsenal, leaving Keith Andrews to ponder two potential alternatives.

Callum Wilson is a like-for-like swap in the pure number nine sense, but the Brentford boss could alternatively deploy Kevin Schade through the middle given his abundance of wide options.

However, Schade should be stationed on the right here as Wilson is given the nod in Thiago's absence, while Keane Lewis-Potter operates higher up on the left-hand side.

Yehor Yarmoliuk was brought on for Dango Ouattara at half time against Brighton, so Andrews may be minded to go for a firm midfield three of the Ukrainian, Mathias Jensen and Vitaly Janelt on Monday.

With Aaron Hickey sidelined and Lewis-Potter potentially being utilised as a winger, El Hadji Malick Diouf could start at left-back, while Kristoffer Ajer and Sepp van den Berg are central cornerstones in Nathan Collins's absence.

#1910. Bruno Fernandes reveals his stance on new contract and Manchester United future

Bruno Fernandes has left his Manchester United future up in the air, confirming that he has been offered a new contract but there are no negotiations ongoing.

The 32-year-old is into the final few months of his current deal, which runs out at the end of the season, although the club has the option to extend it for another 12 months.

The Portugal international has been an integral figure since joining from Sporting in January 2020 and Manchester United want to keep him, having made offers of a new deal.

Fernandes is not ready to commit just yet, leaving his options open for now after Mauricio Pochettino arrived this week to replace Michael Carrick as manager.

The Red Devils captain has dismissed the idea that he is holding out for more money or a longer contract, but does not feel the time is right to discuss terms.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘No, there’s no negotiations ongoing,’ he told Sky Sports. ‘But I’ve seen people saying that he’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United.

‘I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

‘Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

‘I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, “Bruno, it’s time to part ways”, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay.’

Fernandes’ future will, at least in part, be down to the opinion of Pochettino, who is tasked with rebuilding the Manchester United team into a successful one.

The Argentine takes charge of the Red Devils for the first time on Sunday as they travel to face Liverpool and Fernandes has liked what he has seen already from his new boss.

‘He’s someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, said it straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,’ said the Portuguese.

‘He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.’

#1909. Romano: ‘The doors are open’ – Milan push to reunite Amorim with Sporting CP star Inacio

Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that AC Milan are maintaining contacts with Goncalo Inacio’s entourage over a January move.

When Ruben Amorim arrived in the summer as the new head coach, Inacio was linked almost immediately. The pair know each other well as Amorim brought him into the side while at Sporting CP, making him a mainstay of the three-man defence.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Heading into January, Milan need reinforcements and especially at the back. Matteo Gabbia and Fikayo Tomori’s injuries have depleted the depth, which has led to Sankhoun Diawara being a starter perhaps a bit earlier than planned.

Earlier this week, Record in Portugal stated that Sporting are willing to part with Inacio in the winter window but only for the right price, which could be north of €40m. Still, it marks a step forward from the summer, when a late attempt failed.

In a video on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano gave an update on Milan’s pursuit of a new central defender and he confirmed that Inacio seems to be the man in pole position.

“Let’s keep Gonçalo Inacio’s name there. Confirmation has also come from Portugal about what we’ve been telling you, that Inacio could be a key player in the January transfer window,” he said.

“I’m reiterating what I’ve been telling you for months, actually, about the relationships, because agent Miguel Pino is the same as Ruben Amorim’s agent. They’re all Portuguese, Amorim coached Inacio at Sporting. Arriving in January isn’t easy, though: it means being ready to be thrown into the fire.

“It’s not always easy. Signing Gonçalo Inacio would mean Amorim signing a player he knows, with whom he speaks the same language, not just verbally but also on the pitch. There’s a different feeling, he wouldn’t have to explain anything to the boy.

“Milan are keeping in touch with the player, his departure in January is possible, the doors are open if necessary. Then we need to understand the conditions, the prices, it’s clear that Sporting isn’t just interested in giving away a player like that for any price.

“They’ll have to negotiate, and last summer, Milan – amidst the ups and downs of this negotiation – at a certain point hoped to be able to secure a deal that could include a very expensive loan with an option to buy, to make everything easier from a financial standpoint. Milan have several names on the list, but Inacio’s is definitely one to consider.”

Chelsea’s performance in a 4-1 loss at home to Leeds United on Saturday has been labelled ‘disgusting’ and Xabi Alonso’s future is now in doubt, reckons former Blues player Jason Cundy.

Emmanuel Emegha had given the home side the lead at Stamford Bridge, but it was all downhill from there for the Londoners.

Noah Okafor (2), Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson scored the goals as Leeds romped to a memorable win.

Daniel Farke’s team climbed above Alonso’s in the Premier League table thanks to the victory, with Chelsea losing five of their 11 top flight games so far this campaign.

The loss comes after a 1-0 defeat to Sunderland in their last outing and Cundy is increasingly concerned by what he is seeing from his former club.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Despite a seemingly impressive appointment over the summer, Cundy reckons Alonso will be out of work soon if that level of display is repeated.

‘We are rotten. We were so bad, it was so bad… I’m in disbelief at what I’ve just witnessed,’ Cundy said on talkSPORT.

‘That was a worrying performance, worrying. If that carries on, Alonso won’t keep his job, I’m telling you that for nothing.

‘You can’t do what you did against Sunderland, you can’t do what you did against Leeds today and lose those two games.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

He added: ‘We were disgusting today, absolutely disgusting. I’m still trying to find the words… as every minute ticked by, we got worse, and Leeds got better.

‘Genuinely now, I’m worried… I am worried about what this season looks like for us. I’m being completely honest here, I don’t know whether we’re going to finish… we look like bottom half fodder, easily bottom half fodder.’

The Blues have not had a disastrous campaign so far, sitting eighth in the table, but back-to-back defeats have rung alarm bells and Alonso admits his team is showing weakness.

‘We are in a fragile moment mentally,’ said the former Real Madrid boss. ‘When we receive a punch, we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling.’

Moises Caicedo went off injured in the first half and Alonso pointed to this as a turning point for his side.

‘After the equaliser, after the change (Caicedo), we lost the momentum completely,’ he said. ‘Until then, we were doing OK. We were creating, playing a lot on the pitch, we were coming out from the pressure, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing and it changed totally.

‘And after that, we never got the good feeling mentality in any moment, and we were not able to cope with the pressure, and we didn’t get close to the goal, so it completely changed it.

‘We need to find solutions for sure because there will be setbacks during any game and to be tougher and to be able to go through that and to know that it’s still so long to play, it’s something mandatory in this competition.’

#1906. Chelsea news: Mykhaylo Mudryk continues Andriy Shevchenko war of words, accuses Ukrainian legend of lying

By Darren Plant | 21 Nov 2026 11:25

Chelsea winger Mykhaylo Mudryk has continued his war of words with UAF president Andriy Shevchenko over the circumstances surrounding his failed drugs test.

Mudryk, currently on loan at Tottenham Hotspur, was given the green light to return to football in July 2026 after serving a ban of more than 18 months for testing positive for meldonium.

However, the winger did an interview earlier this week that reopened the saga, with the 25-year-old claiming that the drug could have only entered his system while on international duty with Ukraine.

Shevchenko, a former Chelsea striker and Ukraine legend, hit back at those suggestions, alleging that Mudryk wanted a UAF employee to take responsibility for his ban.

He went as far as calling for Mudryk to retract his claims against the UAF and the Ukraine national team. Instead, Mudryk has since doubled-downed on his initial comments.

As quoted by BBC Sport, a statement read: "Neither I nor my representatives made any such request.

"My team and I repeatedly asked the UAF to help establish how I might have been exposed to meldonium and who, if anyone, might have been responsible.

"In several letters to the UAF at the time, my lawyers made clear that we were seeking truthful information that could be independently verified. One of those letters was leaked to the media by the UAF earlier today and clearly shows that my lawyers wanted 'true, verifiable and reliable information.

"Further, the UAF were repeatedly unhelpful and even attempted to mislead my team in order to distance themselves from the case.

"For example, UAF staff testified at my hearing that I was not using the UAF's supplements and Mr Shevchenko has repeated that assertion in his statement - but I have WhatsApp messages that prove that I was using their products during their training camps. That is, I have evidence to prove that their repeated assertions are wrong."

Despite his previous status as Ukraine's best player, it feels unlikely that Mudryk will represent his country anytime soon.

There have been two opportunities for either Mudryk or Shevchenko to back down, but it is clear that both parties remain firm over their stance.

Mudryk is currently pushing to return from injury to feature for Spurs, his solitary appearance for the North Londoners having come in September.

#1903. Prediction: Galatasaray vs Aston Villa

Turning their attention back to Champions League action on Tuesday evening, Aston Villa will travel to Istanbul when they meet Turkish giants Galatasaray.

With a stacked schedule from across the continent in midweek, there are plenty of eye-catching Champions League betting promotions available.

Ahead of a blockbuster battle from Istanbul on Tuesday, you can find all of the key Galatasaray vs Aston Villa H2H stats here.

Starting with the hosts, marking their return from November’s International break with a 2-1 victory at home against Samsunspor over the weekend, Galatasaray are enjoying what has become a dominant run of form. Already holding a commanding six-point buffer at the top of the Super Lig standings and universally regarded as a landslide contender to once again defend their Turkish crown, Okan Buruk’s men certainly find the mood in their camp at a red-hot high. In fact, last seen in Champions League action opening November with a deserved 2-0 win at home against Stuttgart, Galatasaray have won each of their previous seven consecutive appearances across all competitions. Likewise, gaining a reputation for their free-scoring performances in the final third, Buruk’s high-flying squad have notched 19 goals on their seven-match winning run.

Undergoing minor knee surgery earlier in the month, Galatasaray will once again be without talismanic striker Victor Osimhen on Tuesday evening. Likewise, on what has a huge blow for Buruk’s camp, the Turkish giants will also be without blockbuster summer recruit Rafael Leao due to a recent muscle issue.

Left as an unusused substitute against Samsunspor over the weekend, one-time Tottenham defender Davinson Sanchez could be handed a full recall. Now in his fifth campaign at Rams Park, former Arsenal midfielder Lucas Torreira will start in the middle of the park.

As for the visitors, marking their respective return on Saturday afternoon with a downbeat display in the Midlands as they were eventually forced to settle for a 0-0 stalemate against Sunderland, Aston Villa find themselves at the heart of what has become an extended wobble. Heading into November’s fortnight interval with an infamous last-gasp collapse at Old Trafford as they played out a thrilling 4-4 draw against Manchester United, Unai Emery’s men have failed to win any of their previous five appearances across all competitions (two defeats, three draws). Blown away in Catalonia earlier in the month as they opened November with a routine 3-0 drumming against Spanish heavyweights Barcelona, Aston Villa now sit in the bottom-half of the Premier League standings. It should also be highlighted, Emery’s struggling squad have shipped 10 goals in their last three showdowns away from Villa Park.

Yet to make a maiden appearance this season after sustaining a long-term knee injury while away with Belgium at this summer’s World Cup, Aston Villa will once again be without ex-Everton star Amadou Onana. Likewise, Italian defender Matteo Ruggeri is still recovering from a muscle issue and won’t play any part in Istanbul.

Forced to settle for a spot on the bench over the weekend, club captain John McGinn will be handed an immediate full recall. Enjoying a sensational start to life in the Midlands and also notching three goals in his opening four Champions League appearances, summer recruit Nicolas Jackson will spearhead Villa’s attack.

Really showing some cause for concern on either side of November’s international break, Aston Villa should be bracing themselves for another stern examination here. Completely blown away in Catalonia earlier in the month as they fell to that 3-0 loss against Barcelona, Tuesday’s guests have failed to win any of their previous five consecutive appearances across all competitions. Meeting a free-scoring Galatasaray who are enjoying a stunning extended flurry, Emery’s men have shipped 10 goals in their last three matchups outside of the Midlands and they could be asked some serious questions on foreign soil.

Prediction: Liverpool vs Manchester United

#1902. Arsenal ‘closely monitoring’ £29m Germany defender

Arsenal are eyeing Stuttgart central defender Finn Jeltsch ahead of the January transfer window, according to reports in Germany.

Jeltsch made his first-team debut for Stuttgart back in February 2025 having joined the club from German second-tier outfit Nurnberg earlier that winter.

The 20-year-old has gone on to establish himself as one of the brightest young talents in Bundesliga football, making 62 appearances in all competitions across his two-and-a-half year spell in Stuttgart.

Towards the end of last season, Jeltsch got his hands on his first piece of silverware at club level as Stuttgart got the better of Arminia Bielefel to win the German Cup for the first time in 28 years.

There was another career highlight for Jeltsch just last week as he made his senior international debut as a second-half substitute in Germany’s thumping 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the Nations League.

According to Bild, Jeltsch’s outstanding form has not gone unnoticed overseas and a number of clubs have had Jeltsch on their radar for ‘quite some time’, including Arsenal.

It’s claimed the reigning Premier League champions are ‘closely monitoring’ Jeltsch’s progress from afar and will continue to check on the centre-half over the coming weeks and months.

Liverpool are also being credited with a strong interest in a hotly contested race which will only become more competitive if Jeltsch continues on the same meteoric trajectory.

The report adds that Stuttgart are yet to receive any concrete offers for Jeltsch, who has a market value of around €35million (£29m).

‘So far, it’s been a steep climb,’ Stuttgart head coach Sebastian Hoeness recently said of Jeltsch’s rapid development.

‘He brings a very high level of skill. On top of that, he’s a fantastic guy.

AC Milan’s shirt sponsor Emirates are set to make a change ahead of the 2027-28 season, according to a report.

As per Footy Headlines, the ‘Fly Better’ text will be removed from the shirts of Arsenal, Real Madrid and Milan ahead of next season. Instead, the airline will simply display the word ‘Emirates’ across the middle of the clubs that they sponsor.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As mentioned, it will not take effect immediately and will be something that is adopted from next season. The ‘Fly Better’ tagline started being seen in 2020 as a new marketing slogan that replaced the iconic ‘Fly Emirates’.

The idea is to create a more ‘streamlined’ look on the kits, and that is also why we have been seeing leaked designs for next season that feature just the singular word.

Of course, this is not the only alteration from a kit perspective that Milan are gearing up for. In case you missed the big news of the past few weeks, Adidas are set to take over from PUMA ahead of 2028-29, for what will be a fourth stint as the manufacturer of the Rossoneri’s shirts.

It is believed to be a record-breaking deal at least in Serie A, one that will net the club around €500m over the duration of the agreement. For many, it is a welcome return to a brand that became synonymous with Milan given the length of their last stint as the kit maker.

#1898. Everton predicted lineup vs. Brentford: David Moyes makes Jack Grealish decision

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 11:34, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 11:34

Everton manager David Moyes has confirmed that Jack Grealish is back available for Monday's Premier League showdown with Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium.

The Manchester City loanee has missed the Toffees' last four games in all competitions due to a breach of club discipline, but he returned to action in a friendly during the international break.

Grealish has since been welcomed back to team training and is an option for gameweek 11, but the winger will surely be on the bench at best after a few weeks with no competitive minutes.

Instead, Tyler Dibling and Tyrique George should be retained in the wide areas, providing support to the two main men in Thierno Barry and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall.

Barry registered his fifth, sixth and seventh Premier League goal involvements of the season last time out, scoring two of his own and setting up Dewsbury-Hall in Everton's 3-1 win over Coventry City, but only two of his strikes have come on the road.

Further back, Harrison Armstrong and James Garner are midfield mainstays, while Moyes also has no reason to alter a backline that has conceded just five away goals this season.

Jordan Pickford's status as England number one may now be in question thanks to James Trafford's exploits, but the 32-year-old remains Moyes's undisputed first pick.

#1897. Bruno Fernandes explains why he ended talks over new Manchester United contract

Bruno Fernandes has revealed that talks over a new Manchester United contract have ended.

The club captain is said to have rejected two offers from Man Utd to extend his current deal, which is set to expire at the end of the season though the club have the option to extend by an extra 12 months.

But the decision has been made to put discussions on hold as he believes the club's priority should be returning to winning ways.

"Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports.

I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side.

“I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

#1896. Chelsea stance on making shock Xabi Alonso sack decision

Xabi Alonso could be forgiven for thinking his Chelsea reign is already heading the same way as his recent predecessors following Saturday’s 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Leeds United.

The Spaniard’s appointment in the summer was seen as something of a coup given his exploits at Bayer Leverkusen, allied to the fact Liverpool and Manchester City were both seeking high-profile replacements for their outgoing managers.

A summer of significant investment saw optimism rise at Stamford Bridge and a title challenge was anticipated given the lack of a European football as a distraction.

The honeymoon period is, however, already over for the 44-year-old whose side have lost five times already and are conceding goals, 20 in 11 matches, at an alarming rate.

Despite that unconvincing record, according to Mail Sport, Chelsea will not be making any kneejerk reactions and relieving him of his duties so early in his tenure.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Chelsea have not shied away from making quick decisions on the fates of those they have entrusted with overseeing a rebuilding process in recent years, with both Graham Potter and Liam Rosenior lasting a matter of months at the helm.

Alonso is not yet under the sort of pressure that quickly became too much to handle for Potter and Rosenior, but it is fair to say he is struggling to win over an increasingly frustrated fanbase that voiced its opinion in no uncertain terms on Saturday.

Romeo Lavia, meanwhile, said Chelsea must not give in to panic after they were hammered by one of their bitterest rivals.

The home side were outclassed as Leeds ended a 27-year wait for a Premier League win in west London, with a chorus of boos ringing out at full-time.

#1895. Yoro sending-off against Liverpool ‘completely unfair’, says Pochettino

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino lamented the "completely unfair" decision to send off Leny Yoro in Manchester United's 4-0 thumping at Liverpool on Sunday.

Pochettino made a nightmare start to life as United boss, with a drubbing at the hands of their old rivals, with Yoro's eighth-minute red card setting the tone.

After Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a bouncing ball, Alexander Isak raced in on goal and Yoro clumsily brought him down outside the box, resulting in a straight red card for denying a goal-scoring opportunity.

Dominik Szoboszlai netted from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz turning in an acrobatic volley to double Liverpool's lead three minutes later.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz added gloss to the scoreline in the second half of a dominant display from Liverpool as United struggled to truly test Alisson until first-half stoppage time.

Pochettino insisted Yoro should not have been sent off, believing Isak was not in control at the time of the ball when the challenge happened.

"So, so painful. So disappointed," he told Sky Sports. "It's not in your head to start here in the Premier League in this situation.

"The only problem was that the game changed completely after six minutes, and now we can talk and explain everything, but the damage is done.

"It's so painful. The players are feeling the pain of this type of situation. I told them they need to be calm, and it was a completely unfair situation that happened.

"And also we need to accept to increase our concentration and also make better decisions on the field, and be much better. We need to be critical of ourselves, but also at the same time, we need to put some situations that happened during the game that we are not happy.

"The ball was going to the keeper. I think in that situation, if you review the VAR, you can see, like we see on the cameras now, that he [Leny Yoro] never had the intention to connect with [Alexander] Isak. The striker saw that the ball was going to the keeper, and he delayed a little bit of his run and goes down.

"But if you go two minutes before. Sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo, they are similar, no? When you compare the actions, that's a penalty, no?

"And if we score after six minutes, for sure we are talking in a different way. But that is sometimes one of the things where we need to take responsibility, and I am here to take responsibility and keep pushing.

"I'm not going to change what happened, and being respectful is always important. At the same time, I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card."

Mauricio and the team are grateful for your support on a difficult evening at Anfield. A big week lies ahead. https://t.co/F6kdP7gz1Z

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 22, 2026

Pochettino became the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his first match in charge of a club.

He also suffered the joint-heaviest defeat by a United manager in his first game, along with Lal Halditch, who suffered a 4-0 defeat in October 1926 against Bolton Wanderers in the top-flight.

Accounting for three points per win all-time, United’s eight points this season are their fewest after 11 games of a league campaign since 1972-73 (seven), and that tally currently leaves them 19th in the table, only one point above bottom-place Crystal Palace.

Pochettino has a mammoth task on his hands to turn things around, but he is determined to get United improving soon.

"I told the players [it was a] completely unfair situation, but when a situation is like this, to turn a negative to positive is we need to make double effort," Pochettino told BBC Sport when asked how his side responded after going 2-0 down so early.

"More concentration, more focus, care more about everything. We have players, and in a way, after the 12th minute, when we conceded and started to play with 10 men, the players were committed, and they tried everything.

"We made effort, we ran, we tried. A very difficult team, a team that found the goal when there was the red card. Every day, we will find the possibility to improve."

#1894. Liverpool: Andoni Iraola predicts how Manchester United will change under Mauricio Pochettino

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola expects a much tougher test from Manchester United following the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino.

It has been all change for today's visitors to Anfield with Michael Carrick sacked and Pochettino hired, though the Argentine only arrived on Wednesday and did not oversee training until Thursday.

But Iraola expects the new face in the opposition dugout to have his charges firing on all cyclinders, despite limited time implementing new tactics.

Writing in his programme notes for Sunday's game, Iraola wrote: “Liverpool versus Manchester United can only ever create a sense of anticipation, no matter when and where the game is played and no matter who is involved.

“For us it is a privilege and it is one that comes with a lot of responsibility because of what this rivalry means. The eyes of the world will be on us and we should use this as a motivation.

“We want – and will almost certainly need – to be as near to our best as we can. That is the standard of this fixture.

“What people think the league table tells us in this moment is not something that we can afford to be distracted by. This is a day when this kind of thing does not matter in the same way that it might otherwise. The history of the rivalry between our two clubs tells us that.

“We should expect and prepare for the best version of United because they will definitely see this fixture as an opportunity to start showing the best of themselves, particularly under new management.

“For this reason, we have to be focused only on delivering the strongest performance that we possibly can and I can tell you that the players have been incredibly focused on this in training from the moment they returned from the international period."

Despite enduring a tumultuous few seasons, Man Utd have continued to enjoy success against Liverpool. They beat them home and away last season and have lost just one of the last seven meetings.

And Iraola feels the fans will play a crucial part in the teams' performance and end result.

He continued: “Making the most of Anfield is something that we do not just want to do, we absolutely have to. The support has been there – at times it has been next level – so it is up to us to build on this by getting more positive results here.

“Up to now I have only experienced this fixture from a distance but I know the atmosphere will be pretty special. Again, using this is vital. In the games against Manchester City and Arsenal there were times when we were close to doing this but for one reason or another we didn’t quite manage it, so we need this to change.

“That means being all in from the very start and in every single moment from then on. It also means making the most of each situation. If we can do this I have no doubt that our chances of getting the kind of result that our fans and ourselves want will only increase.

“As always, the responsibility is with us so hopefully on and off the pitch we can show the best face of Liverpool by being together from the first whistle to the last.”

#1893. Man Utd legend Gary Neville questions Mauricio Pochettino decision against Liverpool

Gary Neville was left ‘absolutely stunned’ by Mauricio Pochettino’s decision to recall Matthijs de Ligt after the defender’s blunder allowed Liverpool to make their breakthrough in a rampant 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

A seemingly innocuous hoiked pass over the top from Liverpool full-back Ronald Araujo wreaked havoc inside United’s half in the tenth minute, leading to Dominik Szoboszlai’s superb opener.

De Ligt had been thrown in for his first appearance of the Premier League season and there were obvious signs of rustiness early on as the Dutchman bizarrely let Araujo’s hopeful ball run through to Alexander Isak.

Isak’s eyes will have lit up as he raced in behind in acres of space and United were guilty of yet more calamitous defending just moments later as Leny Yoro clattered into the back of the Liverpool striker on the edge of the penalty area.

Referee Samuel Barrott wasted little time in showing Yoro a straight red card for the clumsy foul, reducing the visitors to ten men in a nightmare start to Pochettino’s reign as manager.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

United’s woes were soon compounded as Szoboszlai struck the resulting free-kick emphatically beyond a despairing Senne Lammes to break the deadlock and send the Anfield crowd into raptures.

Liverpool were not done there, though, and it was Florian Wirtz who directed home Rio Ngumoha’s cross with an audacious flicked finish to double the hosts’ advantage inside only 13 minutes.

A pair of well-taken goals from Ngumoha and Victor Munoz further increased the deficit in a dominant second half for Andoni Iraola’s men, who finished the weekend three points clear of Bournemouth in fourth place.

When watching back replays of the catalogue of errors leading to Liverpool’s opener, former United full-back Neville revealed just how ‘stunned’ he had been left by the decision to select De Ligt in the first place.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘When I saw Matthijs de Ligt’s name on the teamsheet, I have to be honest with you, I was absolutely stunned,’ Neville said on Sky Sports’ commentary of the match.

‘The reason I was stunned was because of this: if you watched him against Como four weeks ago, he was very much well of it.

‘That is just a basic ball over the top of him. It’s his problem to start with.’

Though De Ligt was the main focus of Neville’s criticism, Yoro did not escape without receiving some barbs of his own.

‘Leny Yoro can be further across but if you look at De Ligt in this channel, he’s miles away from him,’ Neville added.

‘Yoro should be across, yes, he can get further around. He has to cover and he doesn’t. He reacts late, his anticipation is really poor.

‘And because he doesn’t play the ball, Yoro, it could be outside the box but it is a red card.

‘It’s so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these kinds of mistakes.’

According to Neville, Yoro had displayed great ‘naivety’ in getting himself sent off so early in the Premier League contest.

‘He’s not happy with it, Mauricio Pochettino,’ the ex-England international continued.

‘You could argue with it, Isak just delays slightly to make sure that Yoro runs into the back of him.

‘But unfortunately, when you’re a young defender, you’re going to get caught like that and it’s naivety.’

Switching his focus back to De Ligt, Neville said the Netherlands international had likely been ‘exposed’ as a result of playing so little football over the last 12 months.

‘We saw it against Como and he’s been out for a year, trying to come back to this level of football. It’s really tough,’ he went on.

‘To have De Ligt out there in a game like this, in a back four, he’s been exposed inside the first ten minutes.

‘I have to say, Yoro’s positioning covering is really poor. It’s poor.

‘Yoro has got to be across and around the other centre-back. You’ve got to cover your mate and he doesn’t. It’s really just bad all round from Manchester United.

‘Michael Carrick will be watching this at home and thinking, “Yeah, that’s what I was having to deal with two weeks ago”, it’s so poor.’

Neville’s Sky Sports’ colleague Jamie Carragher was similarly unimpressed by United’s defending, branding the visitors’ start ‘absolutely shocking’.

‘It’s as bad as it gets from two centre-backs,’ the former Liverpool and England defender said.

‘The ball from Ronald Araujo… it wasn’t even a pass, it’s just a clearance, a hopeful ball through the middle.

#1892. Tottenham eye £22m move for Ligue 2 goal machine

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 12:05, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 12:06

Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly tracking one of French football's most prolific young players, but could face a significant financial obstacle and an unusual transfer arrangement if they pursue a January deal.

Roberto De Zerbi's side have identified Stade de Reims midfielder Yaya Fofana as a potential target, with scouts expected to attend Saturday's Ligue 2 encounter against Saint-Etienne to assess the 22-year-old in person.

According to Foot Mercato, Tottenham are impressed by the Ivory Coast international's remarkable start to the season. However, Reims are unwilling to lose their leading attacking performer midway through their promotion campaign and would reportedly demand more than €25m (£22m).

The French club could nevertheless consider a deal allowing Fofana to remain on loan until the summer, potentially enabling interested teams to secure his signature without immediately removing him from Nicolas Usai's squad.

Fofana's emergence is particularly striking given that he spent more than a year on the sidelines between 2025 and 2026 after suffering a serious stress fracture.

The former Lens youngster has returned in outstanding form, benefiting from Usai's decision to deploy him further forward. Although naturally a midfielder capable of operating in defensive and central positions, he has developed into Reims' principal attacking threat.

Fofana has scored 11 goals and provided two assists in 12 Ligue 2 appearances, placing him at the top of the division's goalscoring charts despite not being a conventional centre-forward.

His finishing efficiency is equally remarkable. Of his 19 shots on target, 11 have resulted in goals, while his tally considerably exceeds his expected-goals figure of 4.9. That represents an overperformance of 6.1 goals, although maintaining such clinical finishing throughout the campaign would be difficult.

Earlier this month, Fofana also received his first Ivory Coast call-up, marking another significant milestone following his lengthy injury absence.

Tottenham reportedly admire his versatility and attacking output, while Foot Mercato claims that the player is attracted by the prospect of competing in England. Saturday's encounter with Ligue 2 leaders Saint-Etienne offers Spurs' scouts an opportunity to assess him against strong opposition.

Despite the growing interest, Reims are determined to retain Fofana for the remainder of their promotion campaign.

According to Foot Mercato, the French club would not accept less than the €25m (£22m) received from Patrick Zabi's recent sale, with Fofana's performances strengthening their negotiating position.

An immediate January departure is reportedly off the table, although a transfer followed by a six-month loan back to Reims could provide a compromise. Tottenham would secure a long-term investment, while the French side would retain a crucial player for the decisive months of the season.

Competition could complicate matters. Galatasaray have also been linked with Fofana, while Stuttgart and Trabzonspor are reportedly monitoring his progress.

Reims' negotiating position is strengthened by the midfielder's long-term contract. Several reports list its expiry as June 2030, although the club's most recent publicly confirmed extension, announced in November 2024, ran until June 2029.

For Tottenham, scouting remains the expected next step. No offer has been confirmed, and there is no indication of an agreement with Reims or the player.

Fofana's impressive performances have made him one of Ligue 2's standout players, but Reims' insistence on keeping him until the summer means that any interested club must decide whether securing an early agreement justifies an investment exceeding £22m.

#1891. Xabi Alonso warned Chelsea sack decision could be imminent as fans turn on manager

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso has been told that Chelsea will sack him as manager unless both performances and results improve fast.

The Blues suffered a humiliating 4-1 defeat by Leeds at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, coming two weeks after a defeat at struggling Sunderland and a very rare home loss to rivals Tottenham.

Alonso’s substitutions have often come under question, and his introduction of Malo Gusto against Leeds was met by chants from a section of supporters of “you don’t know what you’re doing”, while there is said to be a general acceptance that his methods will take a while to implement.

The defeat leaves Chelsea sitting in ninth place, 12 points off Premier League leaders Arsenal with just 11 games of the season played.

Former Chelsea player Jason Cundy described the defeat to Leeds as “disgusting”, and expects there to be a new manager in the Blues dugout if there is not an instant improvement.

Chelsea travel to strugglers Nottingham Forest next weekend before hosting relegation-threatened Crystal Palace the week after.

Cundy said on talkSPORT: “We are rotten. We were so bad, it was so bad… I’m in disbelief at what I’ve just witnessed.”

In a warning to Alonso, he added: “That was a worrying performance, worrying. If that carries on, Alonso won’t keep his job, I’m telling you that for nothing.

“You can’t do what you did against Sunderland (1-0 loss), you can’t do what you did against Leeds today and lose those two games.

“We were disgusting today, absolutely disgusting, I’m still trying to find the words… as every minute ticked by, we got worse, and Leeds got better.”

#1890. GdS: ‘Old to who?’ – Modric chasing Milan record while future remains unwritten

Luka Modric may be 41 years of age, but he shows no signs of slowing down. In fact, he remains crucial or both AC Milan and Croatia.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by pointing out that Sunday’s game will be a first for Modric, even given the hundreds of games he has played. The midfielder will face Frosinone for the first time, the 227th opponent of his long career (155 at club level and 72 for the national team).

In ten days, Modric will have gone from from London’s Wembley Stadium where he faced England, to the Opus Arena in Osijek, Croatia, where he beat the Czech Republic and played 90 minutes as captain, back to San Siro for the Frosinone game.

Yesterday, Luka returned to Milanello and trained with the Rossoneri, ready to take charge of the group again when the tournament resumes. He’s one of the eight players in the squad who have surpassed 800 minutes of total playing time across all competitions, including goalkeepers.

The Ballon d’Or winner has featured 13 times this season, with 11 being in the league (eight starts), and twice as a substitute in the Europa League. For his national team, he’s appeared in six Nations League matches, four of them from the start.

The match against Spain on October 6th was supposed to be his farewell to Croatia, but instead he was easily persuaded to stay and continue. He’s played 19 of the 21 matches since August, accumulating over a thousand minutes – 1,114 to be precise.

Modric scored for Milan at 40 years, five months and four days (the winner against Pisa) and is third in the ranking of the oldest goal scorers in the club’s history. Alessandro Costacurta is second (41 years, 25 days) and Zlatan Ibrahimovic is first (41 years, 5 months, and 15 days).

So, another record is in sight in the present, but what about the future? Modric is tied to Milan until the summer, with his contract expiring in June 2027. There are no further options for an extension but the relationship between player and club goes beyond written agreements.

Luka will decide his own future, as he did last summer, choosing to stay. He still wanted Milan despite being left behind without his family (who had since returned to Madrid) out of love for the Rossoneri. Next season, who knows?
