#1889. Mauricio Pochettino slams ‘unfair’ decision after Man Utd’s defeat to Liverpool

Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United were on the wrong end of an ‘unfair’ decision during their heavy Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Pochettino’s reign as United manager began in dismal fashion at Anfield as his side were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.

The defining moment of the match came after just eight minutes as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

Isak’s touch was heavy and United goalkeeper Senne Lammens quickly retrieved the ball but referee Samuel Barrott still deemed a red card to be the suitable punishment.

To make matters worse for Manchester United, Dominik Szoboszlai blasted home the subsequent free-kick to put the hosts ahead.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Liverpool scored again just five minutes later – Florian Wirtz volleying home a cross from the lively Rio Ngumoha.

England winger Ngumoha, 18, scored Liverpool’s third 20 minutes into the second half before Víctor Munoz added a fourth late on.

Pochettino described his first match as Manchester United manager as ‘painful and disappointing’ but criticised the early red card that paved the way for the heavy defeat.

‘So painful. So disappointed,’ Pochettino said in his post-match interview. ‘It’s not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it’s so painful.

‘The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to the calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP

‘We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field. We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.’

Pochettino, who was hired as Michael Carrick’s replacement last week, added: ‘The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

‘When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper; he runs and goes down.

‘In Leny’s case, it wasn’t intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.

‘If you look before, on the sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo. Similar? No. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty.

‘How that changes life, if you score after six minutes. Now, for sure, we are talking in a different way. We have to take responsibility; I take the responsibility. We keep pushing.

‘It’s not going to change what happened. Being respectful is the most important. At the same time, I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel.

‘That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card.’

Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone prior to the November international break, when Carrick was relieved of his duties.

Results over the weekend leave the Red Devils second from bottom in the Premier League with just eight points from their first 11 games of the campaign.

Liverpool, meanwhile, climb back into the Champions League places after an emphatic win over United.

Anfield boss Andoni Iraola said: ‘We have been very good away this season but at home we haven’t been good enough and still haven’t been good enough.

‘We needed a big game, and Manchester United is always a big game, to finish like this.

‘It’s true the game’s condition changes because they play with 10 most of the game, but still we’ve done our job, we controlled the game and I think it’s always nice when you can win like this in these kind of games.’

Asked for his take on the early red card, Iraola added: ‘I think he’s the last man, no? It’s a clear foul and a red card, yes?’

Manchester United and Liverpool both return to Champions League action this week, with the former travelling to Sporting and the latter visiting Club Brugge.

#1888. Bruno Guimaraes breaks silence on Newcastle boos and Arsenal ‘frustration’

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Bruno Guimaraes has reacted for the first time since receiving a hostile reception on his return to Newcastle following his £75m move to Arsenal.

The Brazilian felt Newcastle in the summer, ending a four-and-a-half-year spell which saw him named captain and win the Carabao Cup.

The midfielder’s exit was somewhat acrimonious, so Saturday evening’s return to St James’ Park was greeted to boos every time he touched the ball, in what proved to be an underwhelming performance as the Gunners dropped points in a 2-2 draw.

Bruno Guimaraes is known to be an emotional character, and the reception appeared visibly affect him and was substituted by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta in the 70th minute, being replaced by Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Guimaraes later took to social media to reflect on an emotional evening and his frustration at Arsenal's failure to secure all three points.

"A different experience for me today, returning to a place where I’ve shared so many happy memories over the past five years," he posted.

"A game of two very different halves, and the frustration of not being able to take all three points at a place where it’s always tough to play.

"There's still a lot ahead of us. We keep moving forward together, always!"

Reflecting on the performance, which Standard Sport rated as the worst from an Arsenal player, Arteta said: “We spoke about that before the game because it is emotional when you have so much going on, especially in the way that he feels connected to this club, being the captain and everything that they did together.

“But I think he was very composed. He was very, very, very focused on what he had to do in the game. I think for the time that he was on the pitch, he had a very good performance.”

#1887. Next Swansea manager: Vitor Matos accepts 'anger' from fans over Strasbourg move

By Darren Plant | 21 Nov 2026 12:05

Vitor Matos has admitted that he must accept the 'anger' of Swansea City supporters after his surprise move to Strasbourg.

The Portuguese was deemed to be doing an outstanding job at the Swansea.com Stadium, a consequence of establishing the club in the top six of the Championship table.

However, despite impressing in South Wales and having a long-term contract, it became apparent earlier this week that he wanted to to move to Strasbourg in Ligue 1.

Having indicated a desire to leave Swansea after less than a year in charge, the 38-year-old has faced a backlash from fans.

Speaking at his first press conference as Strasbourg boss on Friday, Matos acknowledged that he had no issue with the reaction to his exit.

He told reporters: "One situation I need to address is Swansea. It was a really hard and tough decision to leave the club mainly because it was a place from the first day, that treated me with all respect and care – me and my family.

"So it was a really tough decision to leave and that's why I needed to thank everyone there.

"Saying that, I really don't expect any good will from the Swansea supporters after my decision. I understand they are angry with that, but it's a club that I love that I worked every day to make better, me and my staff."

Having worked under Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool, it is clear that Matos possesses coaching qualities that are appreciated in football.

However, in a managerial career spanning just 59 matches and 17 months, Matos has twice chosen to leave for positions deemed to be more appealing.

That is not necessarily a good look, and he has taken that risk for a club that have just sacked a Portuguese compatriot after 10 matches.

The argument will be that his impact at Swansea will continue to make him an attractive option going forward, but any future clubs will surely have reservations over handing him long-term contracts.

#1885. Sky Sports commentator apologises to David Raya over Arsenal injury remarks

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

David Raya has been apologised to by a Sky Sports commentator, who has accused the Arsenal goalkeeper of feigning his injury.

The Spaniard was forced off during the second half of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle on Saturday night following a collision with Newcastle forward William Osula.

At first it appeared quite an innocuous incident, with Raya seemingly instigating the contact before falling to the grass. Commentator Bill Leslie suggested that the goalkeeper was exaggerating the incident.

Such a ploy has previously been seen from Arsenal and many other clubs to to give team-mates time to regroup.

But once it had become evident that Raya was in fact hurt, Leslie backtracked.

He said on Sky Sports: "David Raya does indeed look in some discomfort. Apologies if I did him a disservice there because it really didn’t look like significant contact with Osula."

Co-commentator Chris Sutton added: "Raya is holding his arm. It looks like there’s some sort of sprain.

“He is in a lot of pain. It really did look innocuous, didn’t it, the coming together."

Arsenal's medical staff treated the goalkeeper on the pitch before he was helped off, with Kepa Arrizabalaga coming on as his replacement. The incident initially raised questions over whether Raya was attempting to waste time, but it became clear he was struggling with an injury.

Similar confusion was also broadcast on BBC Radio 5 Live, with former Chelsea midfielder Pat Nevin reporting: "He is coming off. I have no idea what happened.

"It looked innocuous. It looked like David Raya knocked into the forward."

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta later confirmed Raya would undergo an MRI scan on Sunday to establish the extent of the problem.

"Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don't know," Arteta said.

#1884. Tuttosport: Leadership and versatility – why Milan are targeting Man Utd’s Bruno Fernandes

Bruno Fernandes seems to be emerging as more and more of a concrete target for AC Milan in the coming months.

Owner Gerry Cardinale has already laid out the guidelines for the next transfer window (and future ones): he is fully committed to investing in strong players, regardless of age, with the aim of returning to competing for trophies.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Milan needd to bring in both talented young players who can shape the future squad, as well as players who can provide the backbone in terms of leadership and experience.

Milan are not only looking for players like Endrick and Nicolo Tresoldi, therefore, but also those who can come into the dressing room and help younger players. The impact Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Simon Kjaer made on the last title-winning team is a good example of this.

Among the names on the shortlist, as reported by Tuttosport, is Bruno Fernandes. His contract with Manchester United is expiring at the end of the season, and the belief is that he could help fill the technical and experience void if Luka Modric departs.

Fernandes is an opportunity to be monitored closely, especially since the 32-year-old Portuguese would like to return to Italy, a country he has already frequented in his career given his experiences with Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria.

Bruno is negotiating a possible renewal with the Red Devils but the Manchester club want to propose a new contract with a lower salary than his current one (around €10-11m per season). There is a €65m release clause in his current contract, the paper adds.

This morning’s edition of the paper adds that the Portuguese star appeals because of his versatility, too. He can play as a deeper-lying midfield player – as he did under Ruben Amorim at Old Trafford – as a box-to-box player and as an attacking midfielder.

The latter is perhaps his preferred role, especially now that he is into his 30s. Interestingly, Amorim has switched from being locked into the 3-4-2-1 seen at United to now using more of a 4-2-3-1 in possession, so in theory there could be an ideal role waiting for Fernandes.

#1883. Florian Wirtz shuts down Arsenal claim after Liverpool thrash Man Utd

Florian Wirtz was quick to shut down any suggestion that Liverpool were spending too much time ‘thinking about’ Arsenal after their 4-0 win over Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start in what was ultimately a mismatch between the two bitter rivals, with the Red Devils proving their own worst enemy and giving themselves a mountain to climb early on at Anfield.

Some calamitous defending from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s tenth-minute breakthrough and saw the latter shown a straight red card by referee Samuel Barrott, a decision that only compounded the visitors’ woes.

The impressive Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s advantage with an audacious finish just three minutes later to send the home crowd into raptures, before a pair of second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz completed the rout.

Having cut a frustrated figure on the touchline for the most part, Pochettino made it clear he was less than impressed by the officiating on show as he faced the media shortly after the final whistle on Merseyside.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The Argentinian will no doubt be desperate to turn the tide when United return to Premier League action at home to Brentford in six days’ time, following a midweek trip to Sporting.

The result ensured Pochettino’s men finished the weekend just one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace, with the Old Trafford giants now leading Europe’s top five leagues for most goals conceded (34 in all competitions).

Liverpool, meanwhile, moved four points clear of fifth-placed Bournemouth and just one point behind Arsenal’s two nearest rivals, Manchester City and Brighton, after ten games.

‘Really good. The atmosphere after the game was so good. We could enjoy it and it was just a nice afternoon,’ Wirtz – named man of the match – said of the victory in his post-match interview with Sky Sports.

‘I feel very good but it’s also because the team develops and gets better.

‘Just being part of this, you also get better, so I’m just enjoying that.’

Asked if he was perhaps benefitting from being coached by Andoni Iraola and Jurgen Klopp at club and international level, Wirtz replied: ‘Both are very good coaches and I enjoy playing under both.

‘They both bring different qualities and I’m just happy and can be happy to have two of these coaches.’

Victory in next Sunday’s Merseyside derby at Everton would see Liverpool move to within four points of Arsenal, who host Manchester City later that same afternoon.

When asked if the 4-0 thumping of United had taken Liverpool to ‘another level’, Wirtz replied: ‘Yeah, it was definitely important today, also for the table situation.

‘I think a lot of teams on top of the table, they didn’t win this weekend so it’s good that we could use the chance.

‘The red card influenced the game a bit of course but we take that, we earned it because of the run of Alex [Isak] so yeah, very good.’

Wirtz was then asked if he was ‘thinking about’ Arsenal and possibility of winning the league this season, and his answer was unequivocal.

It came after the Gunners – the reigning Premier League champions – surrendered a first-half lead to drop points away to Newcastle.

‘Uh, I wasn’t talking about Arsenal… all the teams, I don’t know, from one to three,’ Wirtz responded.

‘So we knew, we didn’t speak so much about it, but I think everybody knew it was a big chance to make some points.

#1882. Iraola tempers title talk despite Liverpool’s thrashing of Man Utd

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Andoni Iraola believes it is too soon to consider Liverpool as potential Premier League title contenders after they thumped 10-man Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday.

Liverpool were helped by Leny Yoro's eighth-minute sending-off for a last-man foul on Alexander Isak, with the Reds using their numerical advantage to ruthless effect.

Dominik Szoboszlai flashed home the free-kick from Yoro's challenge in the 10th minute before Florian Wirtz superbly turned Rio Ngumoha's cross into the net three minutes later.

Mauricio Pochettino, taking charge of United for the first time, introduced Harry Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo in an enforced change to try and bring some more defensive stability, but Liverpool eventually breached the Red Devils' back line in the second half.

Bradley Barcola's blistering run ended with a pinpoint cross for Ngumoha to tuck home, with Victor Munoz coming off the bench to seal an emphatic win eight minutes from time.

Since the start of the 2021-22 season, Liverpool's four wins by 4+ goals against United are the most any Premier League team has achieved against another in all competitions.

It was a result that moved Liverpool back into the top four and within one point of Manchester City and Brighton, who dropped points to Fulham and Hull City, respectively.

Arsenal are seven points clear of Liverpool after drawing 2-2 with Newcastle United, but Iraola was keen not to get carried away with the euphoria of beating the Reds' rivals.

"It's still early days. I think we are missing the two big games we lost here at home between Arsenal and [Man City]. They are making the difference in the standings," he said.

"This is still so early. This doesn't stop because we have a very difficult game against Club Brugge, and then we have the big derby."

4 – Since the start of the 2021-22 season, Liverpool's four wins by 4+ goals against Manchester United are the most any Premier League team has achieved against another. Another. https://t.co/c5BtjVXvlB

Pochettino became the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his first match in charge of a club.

Indeed, it was also the quickest Liverpool had gone 2-0 up in a Premier League match against United, going two ahead after just 12 minutes and 40 seconds.

Iraola is now unbeaten in his seven Premier League matches against United (W3 D4), and even quipped that his players could celebrate at half-time after going two goals in front.

"I think it's a big win; always against United it is a big game," Iraola added. "I think also you can enjoy it; you can see it coming.

"It's difficult to enjoy in the Premier League. Normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit and have lovely moments.

"We have missed some clear chances. In other games you will remember those chances; we've controlled the game, and everything was happening around the box.

"It's a 4-0 that was good for us in the standings but also confidence-wise, trying to get better results here at home."

There was also another standout display from Wirtz, who created 10 chances in open play for Liverpool, the most by a player in a Premier League match since Man City's David Silva against West Brom in March 2015 (11).

Wirtz now has eight goal involvements (three goals, five assists) in 16 appearances across all competitions in 2026-27, with the Liverpool attacker also starring in the international break under former Reds boss Jurgen Klopp with three goals in two games for Germany in the Nations League.

"He's in a lovely moment, and we want to keep him there as much as we can," Iraola said of Wirtz.

"He's in a situation against 10 players where you need players like him to control the situation and see the passes in behind.

"He's also arriving more and not just scoring but being a threat. He's becoming another option, and I'm happy with him."

#1880. Newcastle vs. Arsenal: Why Mikel Arteta should fear "hellish" St James' Park return

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 12:28

Ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash between Newcastle United and Arsenal, Sports Mole site coordinator Ben Knapton warns Mikel Arteta to expect a "horrible" evening at St James' Park.

Newcastle vs. Arsenal is just always one of those really awkward fixtures. The only two modern wins I can remember in the current decade were towards the end of the 2022-23 season and of course last season, that magnificent Merino and Gabriel comeback.

Apart from that, St. James' Park has been a pretty hellish ground for Arsenal. But the stats do not lie this season.

Five points clear at the top, nine wins from 10. Only four teams have had a better start than Arsenal's 27 points from 30: Chelsea in 2005-06, City in 2011-12, City in 2017-18, and Liverpool in 2019-20.

All four of those teams went on to win the title.

By that logic, I think this is Arsenal's title to lose, though perhaps too early to say that definitively.

Arsenal fans should be overwhelmingly happy, but there is always that sense we want more. So many of the wins have been narrow, one-nil victories. The Nottingham Forest win needed a deflected goal. The Hull win needed a rebound.

Hull set up in that 5-4-1 deep block, and Arsenal got a little fortuitous, but they also did not get a penalty that the key match incidents panel later said we should have had.

I was also frustrated at Noni Madueke for spurning that late one-on-one chance. He got caught in two minds going around the goalkeeper, when he should have tried to curl it into the bottom corner.

He was clearly upset with himself afterwards. That said, I do not want to be too critical of Madueke right now, because with Dowman still out suspended, Saka still out injured, Madueke has come to the fore in recent weeks.

He has not hit those same numbers that Saka was putting up a couple of years ago at his peak, but many aspects of his game have come on significantly.

He will start on the right-hand side here, and the Madueke versus Lewis Hall battle will be a fascinating one to watch.

But above all else, Arsenal just need to start blowing teams away. Arteta said as much after the Hull City win. He now has 34 1-0 wins in the Premier League since taking charge, the most of any manager in that period.

Arsenal have only scored five goals in their five away games, so I would not be surprised to see another 1-0 here. I am confident for an Arsenal win, but at St. James' Park there is always that hint of fear.

Under the lights, if the team and the fans get going, it can be a horrible place to visit as an Arsenal fan.

#1879. Jamie Carragher ‘felt sorry’ for Manchester United star during Liverpool defeat

Jamie Carragher says he ‘felt sorry’ for Matthijs de Ligt during Manchester United’s Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Ten-man United were thumped 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Old Trafford manager.

The visitors were reduced to ten men inside ten minutes as Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

If that early blow was not bad enough, Liverpool took the lead from the subsequent free-kick as Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home yet another set-piece goal.

#1878. Mauricio Pochettino has already had one wish granted as Manchester United manager

Mauricio Pochettino has already had one of his first wishes granted as Manchester United manager.

The Argentine arrived in the north west on Wednesday, immediately boarding a plane from Cincinnati after his final match in charge of the United States national team to begin work at Carrington as soon as he touched down.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach takes his new side to Anfield this afternoon to face Liverpool in a tricky first match at the helm.

The 54-year-old revealed in his introductory press conference on Friday that he wanted input in big decisions at United as his tenure wore on, and he has already had one particular request granted in his short spell in the hotseat.

In a round of quickfire questions with the club’s media team upon his arrival, Pochettino was asked whether he preferred team lineups to be formatted in shirt number or position order, with clubs having differing approaches to their pre-match graphics.

United have traditionally plumped for a shirt number-first approach, but when Pochettino’s first team selection was revealed ahead of the game against Liverpool, the Red Devils’ first XI was listed in position order.

It outlined that their new boss had gone for a classic 4-2-3-1 shape, listing Leny Yoro and Diogo Dalot as full-backs, and indicating that Matheus Cunha would play up front rather than Bryan Mbeumo.

United travel to Merseyside this afternoon mired in the Premier League relegation zone, winning just once in their last 11 games.

It was a streak that lost Michael Carrick his job, with the former midfielder sacked a week and a half ago after 303 days in charge.

#1875. Paris FC vs Angers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 21 Nov 2026 12:38

Third-placed Paris FC welcome Angers SCO to the Stade Jean Bouin in Ligue 1 on Sunday, with kick-off at 3pm local time.

The hosts have won four and drawn one of their five home league games, while the visitors are winless in five and sit 17th after Troyes beat Le Havre 3-1 on Friday.

Paris FC have taken 20 points from 10 league games, with six wins, two draws and two defeats, leaving them behind only Paris Saint-Germain on 23 points and Lille on 21 on the Ligue 1 table before the leaders play on Saturday.

Liam Rosenior was appointed on July 7 on a contract running to June 2028, after a 107-day spell at Chelsea that ended with his sacking in April, and his side have scored 17 goals and conceded 10.

The standout figure is Lassine Sinayoko, who joined from Auxerre in the summer and leads the division with nine goals in 10 league games, three of them penalties, to go with five assists.

Sinayoko scored a hat-trick in the 3-2 win at Marseille on matchday three, added two goals and an assist in the 3-1 victory over Monaco on November 1, and then scored the only goal at his former club Auxerre on November 7, with Pablo Pagis providing the pass.

Jean Bouin has been the foundation of the season, as Paris FC are unbeaten at home in the league with four wins and a goalless draw against Lyon, scoring 12 goals and conceding five, and they have now gone seven consecutive matches there without defeat.

Their two league defeats came at Lorient (1-0 on October 10) and Lens (2-1 on October 24), and Rosenior said after the Lorient game that his players had never faced such a low block, which is the one test Angers could realistically set.

Angers have eight points from 10 games after two wins, two draws and six defeats, which leaves them six points clear of bottom side Le Havre, who have lost seven in a row.

Their wins came in a 3-1 victory at Auxerre on August 29 and a 2-0 home win over Troyes on September 19, and since the Troyes game they have drawn 0-0 with Lorient and lost four of five, scoring three goals and conceding 14.

The damage was done by two heavy defeats in a short space of time, a 5-1 loss at Brest on October 10, when Brest posted an expected-goals figure of 3.71 against Angers’ 1.39 and Jordan Lefort was sent off, and a 5-2 home defeat against Marseille on October 18.

The 2-0 loss at home to Nice on November 8 was a different problem, as Sofiane Diop scored in the second minute and Angers created so little that goalkeeper Anthony Lopes, a 35-year-old who joined after Nantes were relegated, needed six saves to prevent a heavier scoreline.

Stephane Gilli returns to the club he coached from July 2023 until his dismissal on February 22, when Paris FC were 15th, and he was appointed by Angers on June 9 on a deal to 2028 after Alexandre Dujeux left for Lorient.

Gilli has said Angers will adjust defensively without changing everything and that emotion will play no part on Sunday, but his attack has failed to score in five of 10 league matches, with Prosper Peter scoring against Troyes and Brest and Amine El Ouazzani against Troyes.

Paris FC will be without Jonathan Ikone, who has a dead leg, and Nhoa Sangui, who has a muscle injury, and neither is expected back until late November, while Adama Camara (hamstring) and Samir Chergui (knock) are doubts.

Rosenior otherwise has a near-complete squad, and at Auxerre he used a back three of Hamari Traore, Otavio and Diego Coppola, with Coppola rated the man of the match by Maxifoot.

Moses Simon and Rudy Matondo provided the width at Auxerre, with Ilan Kebbal and Pagis supporting Sinayoko, who is expected to lead the line again.

Angers will be without Lefort, who is suspended, and Bane Diatta, who is injured, while Oumar Pona was ruled out after falling ill on his return from Mali Under-23 duty.

El Ouazzani is available after returning from injury, and Ousmane Camara and Amine Sbai both took part in training on Friday after being rested on Thursday.

With Lefort suspended, Emmanuel Biumla is expected to partner Camara in central defence, with Carlens Arcus and Kalulu at full-back in front of Lopes.

Trapp; Traore, Otavio, Coppola; Simon, Lopez, Lees-Melou, Matondo; Kebbal, Pagis; Sinayoko

Lopes; Arcus, Camara, Biumla, Kalulu; Belkhdim, Belkebla; Allevinah, van den Boomen, Sbai; Peter

Paris FC have scored 12 goals in five home league matches while Angers have conceded 14 in their last five, and that gap in output makes a home win the logical outcome.

Sinayoko decided the last two league wins, with two goals against Monaco and the winner at Auxerre, and an Angers back line without Lefort will have to deal with him for 90 minutes.

The counter-argument is that Angers beat Paris FC 1-0 in August 2025 and held them 0-0 at Jean Bouin in January, and that Rosenior’s side needed until the 63rd minute to break down a 5-4-1 Auxerre.

Those meetings, however, came when Gilli was still in the Paris FC dugout, and this Angers side has been opened up repeatedly at Brest and Marseille and has scored only three goals in five games.

Lopes should keep the margin respectable, but a side that has failed to score in five of 10 league games is more likely to be shut out than to find a way past Kevin Trapp.

#1874. MN: Numbers highlight strange paradox regarding Milan’s attacking output

The first 11 games of the Serie A season have produced some rather intriguing trends regarding AC Milan’s attacking productivity.

MilanNews recall how – after the important win in Genoa before the break – Ruben Amorim emphasised how this Milan team are still far from the final product he envisioned in the summer, especially in the final third.

The Rossoneri are improving in possession control and chance creation, but they often remain too far from the opponent’s penalty area for most of the game. This limitation has also affected Gonçalo Ramos, who has been forced to drop deeper, far away from the penalty box.

After 11 league games, Milan are only 17th in Serie A for shots on goal, averaging 11.5 per game. Yet, they lead Serie A in average xG per shot, at 0.145. In other words, the Rossoneri do not shoot much, but when they do it is very dangerous.

This is also confirmed by the remarkable individual numbers. Adrien Rabiot has scored five goals from 12 shots, with a conversion rate of 41.7%. Diego Moreira is at 40%, Alphadjo Cisse at 38.5%, and Christian Pulisic at 36.4%.

The notable absentee from this ranking is the player expected to score the most: Gonçalo Ramos. The Portuguese has scored just three goals with 33 total shots and 5.35 xG, meaning a conversion rate of 9.1%. These numbers are far from those of his team-mates.

Amorim continues to defend him, emphasising that the problem lies primarily with the team being too deep. Milan must therefore start to generate more territorial dominance, to allow Ramos to operate closer to goal and for him to be on the end of what is clearly quality service being provided.

#1873. Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United: Red Devils mired in bottom three after nightmare Mauricio Pochettino debut

Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare debut as Manchester United manager as he watched his new side fall to a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

The Red Devils endured a horrendous start to the match, with Leny Yoro sent off inside eight minutes and the hosts two goals up inside the opening quarter of an hour on Merseyside.

Dominik Szoboszlai slammed home the resulting free kick after Yoro had denied Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity, who latched onto a mistake from Matthijs de Ligt, who misjudged a ball clipped over the top.

It was two not long after as Florian Wirtz hooked home with an improvised left-footed volley after Rio Ngumoha had darted beyond Diogo Dalot as if he weren’t there down the left, dinking it into the middle for the German to slot in via the crossbar.

Isak produced a superb centre-forward’s performance but was wasteful with his finishing, and he sliced wide after another De Ligt error in the second half, and he was denied by Senne Lammens, who parried well after a brilliant break through the middle from Barcola.

It was three after the hour, as Ngumoha slotted home a deserved third after Barcola had left Lisandro Martinez for dead, burning away from the recovering Bruno Fernandes before squaring for his opposite winger to slide in the killer.

Substitute Victor Munoz emphatically slammed in the fourth after more superb work from Wirtz, who found the Spaniard having won the ball deep in United territory.

Pochettino could only watch on in horror as the enormity of the task he has undertaken became crystal clear to him. For now, his men sit 19th in the Premier League table, firmly mired in the relegation zone.

#1871. Flick lauds ‘unbelievable’ Barcelona turnaround against Villarreal

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Hansi Flick hailed Barcelona's "unbelievable" comeback win over Villarreal but took issue with some of the referee's decisions.

Villarreal made a stunning start against Barcelona, scoring twice in the first seven minutes through Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi to shock Camp Nou.

Lamine Yamal then missed a first-half penalty to send Barcelona into the break 2-0 down, but they completed a remarkable 10-minute turnaround to claim all three points.

Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez – who had made a mistake that led to Villarreal's opener – pulled Barcelona level before Pau Navarro's own goal finished off the comeback.

This was the first match in which Barcelona had conceded twice in the first seven minutes of a LaLiga match since November 1981 against Real Zaragoza, but Flick was impressed with the response his team mustered.

"When you see the first 10 minutes, we don't start so good," Flick said.

"We took too long with the ball, made two mistakes, and they scored two goals.

"The reaction was unbelievable. I think also in the first half it was top. In the first half, we created a lot of chances, the big opportunity with the penalty.

"In the second half, we looked at what we want to do better: better structure, a clear structure. If we play like this, the opponent gets tired. We scored, I think, three goals in 10 minutes; it was amazing."

Never stop believing. https://t.co/mm7d5s2194

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 22, 2026

Flick was angered with the officials in the match, though, starting with the fact that VAR needed to step in to award the penalty Yamal missed after he was fouled by Oluwaseyi.

Fermin was also sent off while on the bench after being substituted for a comment he made to the fourth official when Anthony Gordon had gone down in search of a penalty.

"If it was another result, maybe I wouldn't say anything," Flick added.

"But seeing this referee, we expected [decisions] like that. I am really happy with the referees, but with this referee I am not.

"Also, the linesman, the fourth official, they're always looking to us. They could handle it differently, speak with us, explain things …But they say nothing.

"I told the team that, if that happens, we just have to play better. And, in the second half, it was unbelievable.

"The hunger to come back and to score the goals, it was fantastic. We played against a Champions League-level team. It was an unbelievable game."

#1870. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Possession: Chelsea 50%-50% AC MilanShots: 18-5Shots on target: 8-0Corners: 7-2

The final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

What a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj

Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

Chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

Chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

Chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and quickly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

AC Milan have a good chance to get a goal back. Musah finds space on the right side of the box and cuts it back towards the penalty spot. He picks out Nkunku but the former Chelsea man wastes the opportunity.

Palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Chelsea have their third and their new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2

The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

The first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

Neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

Then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

The space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

Pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

We will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#1869. “Like Pio Esposito” – Camarda’s impatience questioned by ex-Milan Futuro coach Oddo

Massimo Oddo has admitted that Francesco Camarda has unquestionable talent, but suggested there has been some impatience regarding his development.

Going into the 2025-26 season, the decision was made to send Camarda out on loan to Lecce, where he had a mixed campaign to say the least. He did score his first ever Serie A goal, but played second fiddle for large spells until a shoulder injury saw him miss an extended period.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim arrived and decided that he wished to keep the 18-year-old around, believing that he is ready to be the deputy to Goncalo Ramos, the new club-record signing. The Portuguese is struggling for goals, while Camarda is struggling for minutes, leading to suggestions of a new loan in January.

Oddo knows Camarda well having been the head coach of Milan Futuro during their first season in Serie C and then in Serie D following their relegation. Speaking to La Repubblica, he gave his take on the forward’s current situation.

“The talent hasn’t disappeared, but you have to be patient. I take Camarda as an example, one of the most promising centre-forwards I’ve ever seen,” he said (via Calciomercato.com).

“He couldn’t wait and paid the price for his early leap to Serie A. He should have taken a more gradual path, like Pio Esposito. In general, I’m concerned about the excessive power of agents.”

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

I’ve always believed the Camarda and his agent are forcing Milan to play him in the squad but the reality is that he is not ready for this level. I’ve said multiple times and people here think I am hating on him. Camarda is not on the level of Tresoldi or players like Lamin Yamal. The senior level is nothing like the youth level. He needs to gradually wait until he’s about 21-22 before thinking of the senior level.

It’s very obvious that is what is happening. Camarda still needs to develop much of his game. Is first touch is unplayable, his movement is generally slow and reactive and he’s still very easily forced off the ball. It’s a shame because futuro seems like the appropriate level for him but he’s advisors are blocking that path.

Few players emerging from the youth academy are immediately capable of competing at the senior level; however, a young player can progress significantly in a very short time—potentially surpassing a senior player within just a year. The difference lies in whether a club has a strategy and the patience to nurture its own homegrown talent, as opposed to clubs that lack this approach. Take the example of Palestra: he couldn’t break into the Atalanta squad, yet just a year later, he moved to Chelsea. Do you think he would have developed as much at Atalanta as he did at Cagliari? Muharemović—after two seasons at Sassuolo, he is now at Leeds and valued at 100 million. Would he have reached that level had he stayed at Juventus, watching matches from the stands? There are many such examples. Clubs often try to solve their problems immediately through transfers—sometimes hitting the mark, but frequently missing—spending a fortune on a player, while right under their noses, a homegrown talent goes to waste simply because he hasn’t quite reached that level yet.

#1868. Leny Yoro: Why Manchester United star was sent off vs Liverpool as statement issued

Leny Yoro was sent off to mark a nightmare start for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United manager at Liverpool.

The Argentine head coach could only watch on in horror as his new side were thumped 4-0 at Anfield, thanks to goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz.

The Reds took full advantage of their visitors’ red card on eight minutes, when Yoro was penalised for hauling down Alexander Isak as the Swede sped through on goal.

It stemmed from a Matthijs de Ligt mistake, after the Dutchman, making his first Premier League appearance in over a year after a persistent back injury, misjudged the flight of a clipped ball over the top from Jeremy Jacquet.

Isak seized upon the error, Yoro failed to cover his central defensive partner in time, and the 20-year-old was forced to fell the advancing striker before he could get a shot away at Senne Lammens’ goal.

The Premier League Match Centre explained the decision to send the young French defender for an early bath with a post on its social media channels.

“The referee’s call of red card to Yoro for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO) was checked and confirmed by VAR,” the statement read.

Referee Sam Barratt explained to his video assistant referee: “It's a red card for DOGSO. On-field decision is outside [the box], red card, DOGSO.”

The VAR replied: “Defender bundles into him into the back, gets too tight, I think it's a foul.”

Yoro’s last-ditch challenge ultimately went punished regardless, as Szoboszlai stepped up to slam home the resulting free kick, arrowing into Lammens’ far corner to open the scoring.

The result leaves United mired in the Premier League relegation zone, in 19th place, after just one win in 12 games in all competitions.

#1867. ‘I feel like swearing’: Roy Keane issues damning Manchester United verdict after Liverpool thrashing

Roy Keane was scathing in his verdict of Manchester United after the Red Devils’ 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool.

Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare debut at the helm after his recent arrival at Old Trafford, and he entered a baptism of fire at Anfield on Sunday.

The enormity of the task ahead of him was laid bare for the Argentine, as Andoni Iraola’s hosts ran riot on Merseyside.

Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz got the goals to secure all three points after Leny Yoro’s early red card.

Keane in the Sky Sports studio afterwards lambasted his former side’s performance.

"This team two years ago finished 15th,” he explained.

“We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers. When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making?

"Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had.

"And everyone's coming off the pitch saying four [goals] is not too bad? I feel like swearing.

"I thought United were desperate. So bad.”

He took aim at ex-team-mate and fellow Sky pundit Gary Neville, who had described United’s current predicament as “the worst of it” as Pochettino looks to get his teeth into his new project.

"Neville's ok with 4-0?” Keane asked rhetorically.

"Are you telling me they could have done better? 4-0 is not too bad with 10 men? Has anyone ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done!

"People who played for the club said 4-0 is not too bad? Wow.

"Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish."

The result leaves United 19th in the Premier League table, in the relegation zone, with just one victory in 12 matches in all competitions.

Bayern released a statement after the game, revealing Kane would be out for a "few months" with a "torn syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle".

#1865. Mauricio Pochettino makes unwanted history in nightmare Manchester United debut at Liverpool

Mauricio Pochettino made unwanted history on his debut as Manchester United manager on Sunday.

The Argentine watched on in anguish as his new side were thumped 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield, thanks to goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz.

It started horrendously for the 54-year-old as Leny Yoro was sent off just eight minutes in for denying Alexander Isak a clear goal-scoring opportunity, and that was verified by the Premier League Match Centre on social media.

Pochettino, the former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach, has become the first manager in Premier League history whose team has conceded twice and had a man sent off in the first half of their first match in charge.

There was more positive history for the victors, with Ngumoha breaking the fixture’s record for youngest goalscorer as he slid in the third from Bradley Barcola’s breath-taking break, as the Frenchman squared for his opposite winger to slot home beyond Senne Lammens.

He overtook Michael Owen, who was spotted pitchside on TV punditry duty, at just 18 years and 85 days.

The young England star also became the youngest Liverpool player to score and assist in a Premier League game since Owen on Boxing Day back in 1997, when the striker did the same against Leeds United.

The result leaves Liverpool fourth in the Premier League table, seven points off league leaders Arsenal, while Pochettino’s United are mired in the relegation zone, having won just once in 12 matches in all competitions.

#1864. Rio Ngumoha smashes Liverpool record in Manchester United win amid Cristiano Ronaldo comparison

Rio Ngumoha played a starring role as Liverpool thrashed Manchester United 4-0 on Sunday to hand Mauricio Pochettino a disastrous start to his reign at Old Trafford.

The Reds were on fire at Anfield, with Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Ngumoha and Victor Munoz all on target for Andoni Iraola’s men, who secured a second straight win.

It followed Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card after denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity, as Pochettino watched on in horror from the sidelines.

There was more positive news for the hosts, however, and more specifically, their teenage sensation on the left wing.

Ngumoha, who has caught the eye of England manager Thomas Tuchel with his performances, became the youngest goalscorer in the historic fixture, overtaking Michael Owen as he slotted home the third goal, and he also became the youngest Liverpool player since Owen in 1997 ever to score and assist in a Premier League match.

There is another historic figure whose company he has joined in the history books too.

Now, at just 18 years and 85 days, Ngumoha is in the company of United legend Cristiano Ronaldo, after he became just the second teenager to create three or more chances in a Liverpool vs Man United fixture since records began back in the 2003-04 season.

Before he was substituted late on by Iraola, replaced by fellow goalscorer Munoz, he had registered more touches than any other player on the pitch with 48, and he had twice as many successful dribbles than anyone else (four), terrorising Diogo Dalot down the Liverpool left.

#1862. GdS: ‘Ambitious, surprising, Italian’ – Milan set guidelines for 2027 transfer business

When building a squad it is important to have a vision of the end goal, and AC Milan have exactly that heading into 2027.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by stating that there are no transition years when it comes to Milan. Frequently they have chosen to overhaul the squad in the summer window, and sometimes even in the winter.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For example, 2024 brought Paulo Fonseca with Morata, Pavlovic, Fofana, Emerson Royal, Jimenez and Abraham. Then, 2025 brought Gimenez, then Massimiliano Allegri with Modric, Rabiot, Nkunku, Jashari, and De Winter. Last summer brought Ruben Amorim with Ramos, Moreira, Gila, and Cisse.

A not-so-bold prediction: 2027 won’t be slow. Gerry Cardinale even hinted at this, stating: “We’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic. It will take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.” The two transfer windows? Winter and summer, 2027.

The Rossoneri have two key needs right now: a striker and a central defender. They’ll try to secure them as early as the month after next. Nicolo Tresoldi and Endrick are the names that have been talked about for weeks, but the transfer market has surprises.

The difficulties are well known: Club Brugge do not want to sell their jewel in January unless a €60m check materialises, while with Endrick it seems the will of Jose Mourinho must be taken into account. So, alternative names could emerge for the attack.

A central defender is less of a pressing need. Eight months ago, Milan decided to explore the possibility of signing Virgil van Dijk, who turned 35 in July and is regarded as one of the best of his generation.

A year ago, the conditions weren’t there, but now they might be. Van Dijk’s contract expires in June and he’s always been fascinated by Milan and Italy. It’s complex, but it’s worth a try, and Cardinale seems to agree.

Then there is Gabriele Calvani. He’s Italian, 22, plays for Frosinone, and is expected to start San Siro on Sunday. The Diavolo are interested, just as they are keen on Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio, whom Amorim has already coached and attempted to sign in the summer.

Milan will undoubtedly make some changes to their bench over the next 12 months, aiming to mix young players with experienced players. Filippo Terracciano will leave in January, Vladimirov needs to play, Hutchinson is on loan until June, and Jashari will have to reconsider his future.

It’s certain that some Diawara-like players will arrive, i.e. promising prospects chosen through scouting and data. Markus Krösche – if he becomes the new Head of Football, as is now almost certain – will have extensive powers in this regard.

The idea of ​​making the team more Italian is there, but we know how the market works, making it difficult to plan. Not only that, but some Italians will soon leave Milan too. Above all, Christian Comotto and Francesco Camarda are heading out on loan.

The former seems destined for Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, while it remains to be seen where and under what terms the altter will leave. A loan with an option to buy, leaving Milan free to control the future, probably. To a small Serie A team? Possibly, but a move abroad is possible too.

Belgium and the Netherlands are countries where strikers historically have more opportunities in teams that are younger, while Germany could be another destination. If he takes a flight north, don’t be surprised.

#1861. Spalletti hails Juventus’ team attitude for second-half thumping of Venezia

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Luciano Spalletti says Juventus played like a team in the second half to secure their thumping 4-0 win over Venezia in Serie A.

Juventus were underwhelming in the first half, but blew Venezia away after the break, with the half-time introduction of Nick Woltemade for Kerim Alajbegovic proving to be key.

The German got the scoring started before teeing up Teun Koopmeiners, with Juan Cabal and Randal Kolo Muani also getting on the scoresheet.

Juve eventually finished with 1.8 expected goals but registered just 0.08 of that before the break from their four shots.

But they were a different side after half-time, with this the first time they have scored at least three goals in the second half of a Serie A match since March, when they netted four against Pisa.

"They came on for the second half, making choices, taking decisions, with greater fluidity in the passing, trying to have a team idea," Spalletti told DAZN Italia.

"In the first half, we gave the ball away too cheaply; there was nobody moving from their positions, nobody following the flow of the pass, so it was fundamental the players recognised we were missing something, which we provided in the second half."

This was also Spalletti's 600th Serie A match as a manager, though he did not want to get stuck focusing on the landmark for too long.

"With everything people say, what is your career objective after hitting 600 games?" he said.

"Reaching the 601st is the answer, because anything can happen in football."

FT || Un grande secondo tempo e tre punti nel match dell’Allianz Stadium  @EASPORTSFC @easportsfcit #JuveVenezia https://t.co/cvqjxsVXa7

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 22, 2026

Kolo Muani (10 goals in Serie A) is the sixth French player to reach double figures for goals with Juventus in Serie A.

And against no side has he scored more goals in the competition than he has against Venezia (two, also against Como and Empoli).

He took the penalty, which added the late gloss, with Woltemade handing him the ball.

"Last time, he gave me the ball; we both need confidence," Woltemade explained to DAZN.

"When we have the chance to help each other, we help each other. I don't want to act like I'm a good guy who gave him the ball.

"It was normal for me. He's a good guy; he took the penalty, and he took it.

"It's an important win. After the international break, it's always difficult to find the rhythm again.

"We knew it was a tough game, but I think we did quite well in the second half and scored at important moments."

#1860. Mauricio Pochettino bemoans ‘unfair’ Liverpool incident in ‘painful’ Manchester United defeat

Mauricio Pochettino has called Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat by Liverpool “so painful”.

The Argentine, making his bow as the Red Devils’ latest head coach at Anfield, watched on as his new side were thrashed by Andoni Iraola’s hosts in a one-sided affair.

Leny Yoro was dismissed on eight minutes for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity, and Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz netted the goals that handed the Reds a huge three points, and deservedly so.

Reflecting on the heavy loss, which demonstrated the sheer size of his task ahead, Pochettino bemoaned the red card as a key turning point at such an early moment in the encounter.

"So painful. So disappointed,” the former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach said.

“It's not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after [eight] minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it's so painful.

"The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm. It was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

"We also need to be critical of ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy with."

The 54-year-old identified two reasons why he believed Yoro should not have been sent off, despite VAR validating referee Sam Barrott’s on-field decision to give the French defender his marching orders.

"The ball was for the goalkeeper,” Pochettino explained.

“In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

“When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down.

"In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.

"How that changes life, if you score after six minutes. Now, for sure, we are talking in a different way. We have to take responsibility, I take the responsibility. We keep pushing.

"It's not going to change what happened. Being respectful is the most important. At the same time, I have to defend my club and tell what I feel. That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card."

#1858. Gary Neville delivers scathing Manchester United verdict after heavy Liverpool defeat

Gary Neville believes there has been a “remarkable” drop in Manchester United’s standards after the Red Devils sank to a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday.

The club were looking to propel themselves out of the Premier League relegation zone, helped by a bounce from the arrival of new manager Mauricio Pochettino, who took charge of his first match at Anfield.

The Argentine, however, was dealt a nightmare start, as Leny Yoro was sent off inside eight minutes for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity, and Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz got the goals for Andoni Iraola’s brilliant hosts.

Pochettino bemoaned Yoro’s red card as “unfair” in his immediate post-match reaction, but he could not complain about his side’s performance on the night, as they were swept aside emphatically by their historic rivals.

On Sky Sports, former United defender Neville said that Pochettino had now seen “the worst” of his new club’s predicament.

“It's really desperate and it's tiring watching them,” he said.

“This is the worst Manchester United have ever been in 53 years.

“There's no time to work on this. Maybe this will be a good thing in the long run that Pochettino sees the worst of it.

"He's got a big job on here. There'll be an element of 'Let's just forget about this game because Yoro got sent off and it's with 10 men', but it rides into the game in midweek.

"From a defensive perspective, I've never seen anything like this.

"I grew up watching great defenders that were fantastic players that were aggressive. They were brilliant people, great fighters and had spirit.

"You watch this lot, honestly, it's unbelievable. They're going to have to advance money to [Pochettino] in January for defenders. They're probably going to need another couple next summer.

"Forget the rest of the squad for now, they've got to build from the back.

"Manchester United are the worst team in Europe defensively right now. You can't say anything more than that. It's unbelievable. 34 goals [conceded] in 15 matches.

"This is where we've got to where we're starting to write off 4-0 defeats at Anfield as if it's just the norm and what should be accepted.

"The club standards have dropped so far, it's incredible.

"But the fans’ standards haven't dropped. They expect a Manchester United team to be competitive every single week, and what they're seeing now, Manchester United have got the worst defence in the whole of Europe, and are currently second from bottom in the Premier League.

#1857. Andoni Iraola fires jab at Mauricio Pochettino after easy Liverpool win over Manchester United

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said his side could “celebrate at half time” during their 4-0 win over Manchester United.

The Reds ran out easy victors against their fierce rivals on Sunday, with United hoping to snap a miserable run of just one win in 12 matches.

They did not get the desired bounce from the arrival of new boss Mauricio Pochettino, who watched his side thrashed at Anfield and go down to ten men in eight minutes after Leny Yoro’s red card, which he bemoaned afterwards.

Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz netted the goals to hand the hosts a straightforward three points that sees them sit fourth, seven points off league leaders Arsenal.

United, meanwhile, are spiralling and remain in the Premier League relegation zone, in 19th place.

Iraola seemed to fire a jab at Pochettino and United in his post-match interview.

"It's a big win, always against United it is a big game,” he said.

“I think you can enjoy it, you can see it coming. It's difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half time and enjoy it a little bit and have lovely moments.

"We could have scored more. We missed some clear chances today. In other games you will remember those chances, today we've controlled the game and everything was happening around the box.

"It's a 4-0 [win] that was good for [our confidence], trying to get better results here at home."
